<a id="chapter-20-target-abi-profiles"></a>

## CPN26 Target ABI Profiles Specification

Static reflection handles, syntax quotations, and generated-declaration values have no native ABI representation. A generated ordinary native declaration is ABI-checked exactly as a source-authored declaration under its owning module and target profile. Reflection of a foreign declaration is limited to properties made available by the verified foreign ABI descriptor; inferred type layout or compiler metadata identity cannot establish unverified direct C++ compatibility.

### 1. ABI compatibility is a versioned contract

A CPN26 native object is interoperable with a C or C++ object only to the extent specified by the **selected target ABI profile**, matching foreign declaration contracts, and required support libraries. The extension `.o` or `.obj` does not determine object format. A conforming implementation of a target profile shall emit an ordinary, machine-code-containing relocatable object suitable for the target's standard linker without mandatory CPN26-specific LTO support.

Direct ABI compatibility shall be established by the relevant declared type, call, lifetime, and effect contracts. Direct C++ interoperability additionally requires a selected C++ ABI provider; an exact library ABI contract is additionally required only for the foreign library types or operations actually crossing that boundary. Opaque adapters remain valid when direct class representation is unavailable or incompatible.

This chapter owns the target-family and capability catalogue and applies Chapter 09's foreign declaration and lifetime model. All profiles below identify **families** of target contracts. The selected object/linking, unwinder, CRT, and ABI-provider contract revisions shall bind the compilation; explicit `none` shall supply an absence binding. Producer compiler and actual tool-input versions shall enter build context independently of the public ABI contract. The [reference native bindings](#chapter-30-reference-target-bindings) supply complete baseline instances. A selected standard contract export shall use the exchange fields in the [public schemas](#chapter-29-public-contract-schemas).

### 2. Standard target families

A conforming implementation may support any declared subset of the following target families. A program requiring a family that the toolchain does not supply receives `ERROR` rather than a substitute output format.

| Profile family | Pointer model | Native relocatable format | Default C data model | Native platform calling convention |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x86_64-linux-sysv-elf` | 64-bit pointers | ELF64, x86-64 | LP64 | System V AMD64 psABI, plus selected Linux supplement |
| `aarch64-linux-aapcs-elf` | 64-bit pointers | ELF64, AArch64 | LP64 | AAPCS64 with selected Linux ELF supplement |
| `x86_64-windows-msvc-coff` | 64-bit pointers | AMD64 COFF/PE rules | LLP64 | Microsoft x64 convention |
| `aarch64-windows-msvc-coff` | 64-bit pointers | ARM64 COFF/PE rules | LLP64 | Microsoft ARM64 ABI convention |
| `x86_64-apple-darwin-macho` | 64-bit pointers | Mach-O x86-64 | LP64 | Apple x86-64 ABI |
| `aarch64-apple-darwin-macho` | 64-bit pointers | Mach-O arm64 | LP64 | Apple arm64 ABI |

The existing names `x86_64-sysv-elf`, `x86_64-msvc-coff`, and `darwin-<architecture>-macho` may be retained as **profile aliases** only when they resolve to one unique fully qualified family and a fixed revision. An alias that is ambiguous between Linux, another ELF operating system, or incompatible CRTs is not valid at a shared ABI boundary.

Linux targets further declare the C runtime family, such as glibc or musl, and its relevant ABI compatibility contract. Windows targets declare the MSVC-compatible compiler/CRT contract, including static/shared CRT selections when they affect allocation and exception handling. Apple targets declare the SDK/platform deployment contract and the relevant Darwin ABI. Changing any of these on a binary boundary is not a silent source-level configuration override.

### 3. Core foreign scalar correspondence

For the six **standard 64-bit profiles above**, the common C scalar sizes in octets are:

| Foreign scalar | Linux LP64 | Windows LLP64 | Darwin LP64 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `ffi::c_short` / `ffi::c_ushort` | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| `ffi::c_int` / `ffi::c_uint` | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| `ffi::c_long` / `ffi::c_ulong` | 8 | 4 | 8 |
| `ffi::c_llong` / `ffi::c_ullong` | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| C pointer and `size_t` equivalents | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| `ffi::c_float` | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| `ffi::c_double` | 8 | 8 | 8 |

These widths are **not** native aliases: even when two foreign scalar types have the same storage width, their nominal C identities can differ. Native `i32`, `i64`, `usize`, and CPN26 `char` do not automatically acquire C argument-passing or C++ name-mangling identity. In particular, native Unicode-scalar `char` is not `ffi::c_char` or the platform's `wchar_t`.

The target descriptor additionally binds:

- whether plain C `char` is signed;
- `_Bool` and foreign `bool` size, alignment, canonical representations, and parameter-passing rules;
- `wchar_t`, `char16_t`, `char32_t`, foreign enumeration and bit-field representation;
- `long double` format, precision, exponent range, storage, alignment, and calling convention;
- signed/unsigned extended integer and compiler vector type ABI, if enabled;
- the address-space and function-pointer representation, including any pointer authentication or capability tagging policies.

A caller cannot assume that `ffi::c_long_double` is `f64`, `f80`, or `f128` solely from the CPU architecture. The provider declares the actual ABI type and its conversion contract. Cross-width conversions obey existing CPN26 Checked/Exact and explicit representation operations, not a C-style silent narrowing rule.

### 4. Calling and object-file classification

#### 4.1 Cross-platform rule

A supported ABI profile must bind its call and return classification to the **pinned normative revision of the platform ABI**, including parameter/return register selection, by-reference aggregates, hidden result pointers, stack alignment, varargs, red-zone/shadow-space rules, unwind tables, and TLS models. A direct foreign call shall use that bound platform classification.

Scalar C type identity, aggregate field layout, by-value calling classification, and emitted symbol decoration are checked independently. Even a C-compatible in-memory record is not necessarily passed by value identically across different target ABIs. An ABI descriptor shall include packing and compiler switches that affect records, bit-fields, vector types, or empty aggregate handling.

#### 4.2 Windows x64

The standard Microsoft x64 profile uses the platform's prescribed register/stack parameter classification and reserves the required caller-provided shadow store. It does not apply the System V AMD64 red-zone or aggregate classification. Its C long type follows LLP64. An `extern "C"` declaration uses the selected Microsoft x64 calling convention and native C naming rule unless a compatible explicit alternative is selected in the binding descriptor.

#### 4.3 Windows ARM64

The standard Microsoft ARM64 profile binds to the Windows ARM64 ABI rather than assuming that generic AAPCS64 alone describes Windows exceptions, varargs, unwind records, or platform-specific calling rules. Its C long type follows LLP64. A Windows ARM64 use shall require its supported instruction, vector, and exception capabilities; an unavailable requested capability yields ERROR.

#### 4.4 Linux x86-64 and AArch64

The Linux x86-64 profile uses the selected System V AMD64 psABI and Linux ABI supplement. The Linux AArch64 profile uses the selected AAPCS64 and Linux ELF supplement. Both are LP64 in the standard profiles named here. Their C++ provider, libc family, and C++ standard-library ABI are recorded independently; identical ELF files do not establish that two implementations can exchange C++ `std::string`, exceptions, or allocator ownership.

#### 4.5 Apple x86-64 and arm64

Apple profiles use Darwin Mach-O, selected Apple platform call conventions, and the declared deployment target. Apple's arm64 ABI has platform-specific differences from generic AAPCS64, including stack-argument placement and caller extension of narrow integer arguments. A generic AAPCS64 code path is not evidence of Apple arm64 call compatibility. The provider's supported C++ ABI subset, library ABI, constructor/destructor entry behavior, and exception bridge remain explicit.

### 5. Direct compatibility levels

A target/provider shall publish each supported capability independently:

| Level | Required guarantee |
| --- | --- |
| `native_object` | Linker-readable ordinary relocatable object with declared symbols, relocations, sections, and required unwind metadata. |
| `c_call` | Correct calls/returns of supported foreign scalars, pointers, and function pointers under the declared C ABI. |
| `c_record` | Verified layout and by-value/by-reference handling of the declared C record subset. |
| `c_callback` | Reverse calls and callback storage, ownership, and lifetime under the declared C ABI. |
| `cpp_symbol` | Provider-matching mangling/decoration for a declared set of C++ symbols and overloads. |
| `cpp_class` | Provider-matching class layout, bases, virtual bases, member pointers, virtual dispatch and this adjustment for the supported subset. |
| `cpp_lifetime` | Compatible construction, base/complete/deleting destructor entry points, ownership, and construction-failure rollback under the supported subset. |
| `cpp_rtti` | Provider-compatible RTTI identity and required dynamic-cast/type-identification operations. |
| `cpp_exception` | Provider-compatible exception record, handler search, cleanup, matching, rethrow, and cross-boundary propagation where explicitly enabled. |
| `cpp_stdlib` | Individually verified binary layouts and semantics for named C++ library types and ABI versions. |

For example, support for `cpp_symbol` is not support for `cpp_class`; successful calls to an opaque wrapper are not evidence of `cpp_rtti`. The standard library's own `std::collections::Vector<T>` is not a C++ `std::vector<T>` ABI merely because both have similar public operations.

A provider shall declare feature-level exclusions, including unsupported inheritance forms, member-pointer models, passing or returning nontrivial classes, variadic templates, sized/aligned deletion, or cross-language exception propagation. An exclusion is not repaired by a compiler warning or by assuming a common compiler vendor.

### 6. Native and foreign exceptional control flow

Non-unwinding boundaries and terminal events shall follow Chapter 09's foreign routing contract.

`extern "C++"` alone does not authorize C++ exception propagation through CPN26 frames. A direct `cpp_exception` profile additionally supplies compatible exception object identity, handler-matching rules, stack unwind/cleanup behavior, runtime personality functions or equivalent, and rethrow semantics. A foreign C++ destructor may terminate according to its foreign contract; a CPN26 destructor in Release still follows the CPN26 Release termination rule where that boundary applies. Each entry shall retain its bound destruction/failure policy.

An explicit adapter may translate a supported C++ exception to a declared CPN26 `Result` error. An adapter that raises a translated CPN26 exception shall advertise that native throwing effect and perform the translation within a permitted native propagation phase; no exception crosses a boundary declared non-unwinding. Translation changes primary identity unless the provider specifically supports retaining and propagating the compatible original foreign record. Error payloads with allocated storage have a declared allocator and destroy/release owner. The [error and recovery specification](#chapter-28-error-recovery) defines these distinctions. A foreign `longjmp`, forced unwind, OS exception, or asynchronous cancellation is not implicitly safe across CPN26 frames.

### 7. Native record and ownership binding

`[[abi_layout("C")]]` and `[[abi_layout("C++")]]` attach only the explicitly supported target-provider layout and its required qualifiers. The emitted record shall contain exactly that declared layout. Where CPN26 requires state not represented in a foreign object, it may maintain that state externally or in a separate explicit wrapper without changing foreign field offsets.

A foreign class's constructor/destructor entry points discharge their **actual foreign obligations**. A complete-object destructor cannot be followed by a second CPN26 member/base destructor run; a deleting destructor may additionally free the foreign allocation. The binding descriptor records which responsibility is discharged by each entry. Virtual-base responsibility and early base destruction remain governed by the existing CPN26 lifetime contract and are directly enabled only if the foreign contract genuinely supports them.

Cross-boundary storage transfer identifies an allocator domain and compatible disposal function. Equal raw pointer width does not authorize invoking a different C runtime's `free`, unrelated `delete`, or an allocator with a different resource protocol. Foreign library code and associated RTTI, vtables, callback, allocation, or exception-support records remain loaded as long as an outstanding owner requires them.

### 8. Object emission, static initialization, and module metadata

The target object shall include all sections and relocations required by the selected static-initialization, TLS, unwind, and exception contracts. Object retention and link inputs shall preserve reachable native construction and static initialization obligations through archive extraction and section collection. The resolved link contract shall identify required retention/entry mechanisms and support libraries, with standard external serialization supplied by a selected contract export.

The native initializer graph and foreign CRT's own init/fini mechanisms remain separate unless explicitly mapped. One domain owner is responsible for executing each mapped initialization unit once, with reverse logical destruction for committed CPN26 objects. Each foreign destruction obligation shall have one registered owner.

A native interface's signature, type identity, relevant numerical evaluation configuration, and ABI contract shall determine its resolved boundary identity. A direct boundary shall establish equality of its relevant contract fields; a mismatch shall yield ERROR. Standard export shall encode this identity in Chapter 29's boundary projection and fingerprint. A versioned adapter may explicitly translate representationally compatible values with a declared loss/ownership/failure contract.

### 9. Required ABI evidence and diagnostics

A provider claiming one of the levels in Section 5 shall publish a versioned contract including the applicable reference ABI revision and named supported features. Each required public boundary is either:

- **directly compatible**, with matching specified representation, call classification, effects, and lifetime;
- **adapted**, with a declared wrapper and conversion/ownership contract; or
- **unsupported**, in which case direct use is `ERROR`.

An unverified programmer assertion permitted by the configured boundary policy yields `ANOMALY` and preserves its runtime responsibility; it is never recorded as a verified fact. A compiler cannot declare direct compatibility merely because the host linker accepted the symbols.

Target support dependencies shall follow the core capability model. The ordinary target linker shall resolve emitted machine code using the selected dependencies published by that binding.

<a id="chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance"></a>

## CPN26 Core Execution and Conformance Specification

### 1. Normative model and definition ownership

CPN26 specifies CPN26 source and execution under the bound standard designation, resolved configuration, target contract, and selected providers. An implementation **shall** realize an execution admitted by that combination. **Shall** defines a requirement; **may** identifies a permitted implementation choice. An admitted choice **shall** preserve the observations selected by the operation contract.

The language is native and manually manages storage ownership. Runtime support **shall** follow capabilities actually used by the program. Ordinary native scalar code requires its target's execution and terminal mechanisms. Allocating values, tracked handles, language exceptions, tasks, runtime descriptors, and other selected facilities add their declared dependencies. Low-level operations use the same language and declaration model throughout.

The following table assigns each shared definition one normative owner. Feature chapters **shall** apply these definitions and specify their additional inputs, transitions, results, and effects.

| Definition | Normative owner |
| --- | --- |
| Execution, observation, and transformation permissions | This chapter. |
| Configuration keys, defaults, scope, and diagnostic categories | [Configuration](#chapter-08-runtime-configuration). |
| Object states, initialization plans, and destruction responsibility | [Construction execution](#chapter-06-construction-execution). |
| Source sequencing, storage, pointer access, and control transfers | [Core memory and control](#chapter-12-core-memory-control). |
| Integer domains, common type, and arithmetic projection | [Integer types](#chapter-02-integer-bigint), with expression binding in [numeric expressions](#chapter-07-numeric-expressions). |
| Numeric status, error identity, rounding, NaNs, and tininess | [Numeric integration](#chapter-04-numeric-integration). |
| Coherence, synchronization, and task execution | [Concurrency](#chapter-13-concurrency-memory-model). |
| Common library invocation, ownership, and guarantees | [Standard library](#chapter-14-standard-library). |
| Explicit exception recovery and phase routing | [Error and recovery](#chapter-28-error-recovery), using Chapter 08's record and process policy. |
| Effects, predicates, and callable boundaries | [Contracts](#chapter-24-contracts-effects) and [effect composition](#chapter-25-effect-composition-boundaries). |
| Generation phases and publication | [Compile-time generation](#chapter-23-compile-time-generation). |
| Logical declaration identity and compilation boundaries | [Modules and compilation](#chapter-11-modules-compilation), including the Core root-unit model. |
| Optional public contract encoding and fingerprints | [Contract schemas](#chapter-29-public-contract-schemas). |

A cross-reference imports the owner's rule. Examples illustrate that rule under their stated contract. An explicit operation signature, policy, and result **shall** take priority over an ambient ordinary-operation default.

### 2. Binding and execution

#### 2.1 Source edition binding

Each compilation request **shall** explicitly bind its source edition through the compiler invocation or build-target description before source parsing. A CPN26 request **shall** select this standard's grammar, preset defaults, and semantic rules as one binding. The request **shall** retain that edition in its internal compilation identity and in any exported source-semantic record. Named presets choose configuration within the selected edition.

An unsupported edition **shall** yield ERROR before declarations are accepted. An implementation may support several explicitly selected source editions. Edition selection **shall** follow the declared request; successful parsing of an alternative edition establishes no selection. Imported source or interfaces **shall** retain their declared edition and use an explicitly supported translation or boundary contract when joining another edition. The edition binding applies equally to Core root units, jointly compiled modules, and separate compilation. Its enforcement uses the compilation request and internal identities independently of `tooling.contract_export`.

#### 2.2 Operation binding and phases

Before runtime evaluation, the implementation **shall** determine declarations, types, overloads, generic arguments, explicit contracts, and effective configuration. Generated declarations **shall** pass the same source rules as authored declarations; each generation transaction publishes one validated batch. Imported definitions and generic recipes **shall** retain their published binding during specialization and inlining.

Source typing **shall** determine the result type before testing its target availability. Enabled integer widths therefore test the materialization of the canonical common type defined in Chapter 02. Required constraints, kind matches, and constant evaluation are source decisions. Optional diagnostic analysis supplies additional evidence after those decisions.

Each invocation **shall** follow the phases required by its feature contract:

| Phase | State transition |
| --- | --- |
| Bind | Select the operation, representation, policy, and resources. |
| Evaluate | Evaluate operands and arguments in source order, producing values and source effects. |
| Admit | Establish the stated domain, capability, access, and resource conditions using the selected validation mode. |
| Prepare | Compute a candidate result and acquire tentative resources. |
| Commit | Publish the stated value, lifetime, ownership, progress, or synchronization transition. |
| Retire | Discharge remaining obligations on that returning path. |
| Deliver | Return a value/error, propagate a selected exception, or perform the terminal action. |

Equivalent phases may be combined. A partial-progress interface identifies its intermediate commits; a transactional interface identifies one commit. Argument effects precede admission. A recovery guarantee covers the state named by its operation, while earlier committed external effects remain part of the execution.

The abstract state describes live object generations, storage/release ownership, values and selected status, control flow, synchronization, tasks, and native bindings. An implementation **shall** realize these facts through control flow, registers, locals, explicit objects, provider records, or compile-time information as needed by selected observations. A state description alone imposes no object header or universal registry. Statically determined cleanup can use direct calls; partial array rollback can use a prefix count; explicit dynamic ownership transfer can carry its current owner.

### 3. Observations and transformation permissions

| Observation | Required when selected |
| --- | --- |
| Value | Committed representation, returned value, or permitted numerical result set. |
| Lifetime | Constructor/destructor effects and discharge or transfer of responsibility. |
| External effect | I/O, foreign calls, volatile/device accesses, and callbacks at their sequencing points. |
| Synchronization | Atomic modification order, reads-from relationships, fences, and publication. |
| Numerical status | Local reports and environment state exposed by an observing contract. |
| Failure | Declared error payload, catchable propagation, or terminal outcome. |
| Resource | Selected admission, retained charge, ownership transfer, and release. |

A transformation **shall** produce an execution within the contract's permitted observations. The compiler may eliminate unobserved work, combine equivalent transitions, select permitted schedules, or use a relaxed numerical result relation granted by the bound profile. Timing and register allocation are implementation properties except where an explicit contract states a bound.

Strict equivalence includes the selected result and events. Native equivalence uses the broader target-declared result, environment, and fault contract. Native freedom is available at binding time and requires no proof that a stronger strict contract would be unobserved.

#### 3.1 Release execution

Release presets **shall** select Native ordinary numerical execution, contract-based raw access, and local construction/effect analysis through Chapter 08's default table. Optional diagnostic instrumentation executes when enabled. Feature deltas are:

| Facility | Native execution |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary fixed integers | Chapter 02's Native projection and target-domain behavior; validation branches are optional. |
| Ordinary floating operations | Target arithmetic and declared relaxations, native NaN/subnormal behavior, and unobserved local/sticky accounting. |
| Ordinary Complex arithmetic | The selected scalar-step/provider operation with bound component policies. |
| Pure masked arithmetic | Compute-and-select for inactive lanes whose additional work contributes only discarded values and unobserved numerical state. |
| Construction and effect analysis | Local control flow and bound declarations/summaries; cross-procedure inference is an enabled enhancement. |
| Raw-access and contract diagnostics | Programmer obligations under their selected contract; instrumentation follows explicit configuration. |

Source operand evaluation, memory access, callbacks, device effects, ownership, and atomic synchronization remain observations of the functions that request them. A masked memory operation **shall** follow its active-lane access contract. A checked/reporting vector operation **shall** collect the events required by its interface. Pure Native arithmetic uses the wider permission above.

#### 3.2 Explicit functional contracts

An explicitly named checked, Result, report, exact, wrapping, saturating, tracked-pointer, resource, synchronization, or recovery operation **shall** perform its declared function in every preset. Explicit Strict/Reproducible and accuracy selections establish their stated contracts. Checks may be combined or proved redundant while preserving those results. Cost belongs to the capability selected by source.

A Native caller can invoke a strict function under that function's binding. A strict caller using a native floating boundary **shall** select an adapter or provider guarantee that isolates the native environment effects relevant to its strict observations. Isolation belongs to the stronger boundary; Native entry/exit itself requires no general save/restore wrapper.

A Native status read observes the provider state defined for that interface. Attribution of individual earlier Native operations is outside that observation contract. A source requiring attribution **shall** select reporting operations or a strict observation region before the work.

### 4. Lifetime, resources, and numerical execution

An object generation **shall** identify one lifetime in an authorized extent. Reusing an address creates a new generation. Pointer access **shall** satisfy its generation, extent, alignment, qualification, and access contract. Tracked access realizes its explicit interface; raw access uses the programmer's bound contract.

Each pending destruction action **shall** have one controlling responsibility. Transfer changes that controller. Storage ownership separately identifies release responsibility. Chapter 06 defines admitted transitions and remaining-cleanup order. A returning failure **shall** preserve the invoked operation's promised state; catchable construction failure retires its selected completed subobjects. A terminal action ends the execution path at that point under the target's terminal contract.

An allocating operation **shall** charge actual retained resources under its selected domains and geometry. Optimized preparation and transfer **shall** preserve admission, accounting, and release results. Chapter 14 defines common guarantees; Chapter 32 adds reservation and temporary-epoch rules.

Numeric binding **shall** determine common type, mathematical operation, projection, status, and delivery. A numeric Result **shall** describe its invocation, including repeated events already present in history when local reporting is selected. Constant evaluation **shall** use its target-format contract and isolated compile-time state. A constant Result error is a successful value of its Result type. Native runtime folding uses the Native result set; strict folding reproduces strict observations.

### 5. Concurrency and program images

Shared accesses **shall** follow Chapter 13's location, happens-before, and race rules. An atomic read **shall** obtain a value from a permitted producing modification. Synchronization preserves actual reads-from relationships; bit equality alone establishes value equality. Cancellation and completion **shall** publish the single outcome selected by their atomic commit protocol.

A raw-lifetime or data-race violation leaves the portable contract at the violating action. Target behavior applies from that point. The implementation **shall** preserve preceding valid observations and use an explicitly trusted contract for stronger source assumptions. Native numerical domain outcomes remain the provider's declared fault/result choices rather than evidence that the input was unreachable.

Providers **shall** state their progress guarantees and conditions. Join/close results **shall** identify retained or transferred responsibility. Each program image or independent lifetime domain **shall** have one startup owner and static dependency graph. Initialization commits logical positions; normal shutdown **shall** retire committed statics in reverse logical order. Concurrent startup uses the graph's cancellation/commit protocol.

An image **shall** retain required code and support while live values, callbacks, releases, exception records, or tasks depend on them. Foreign startup relationships use explicit mapped dependencies or independent host lifetimes. Native compatibility follows the declared ABI feature subset.

### 6. Diagnostics and conformance

The compiler **shall** apply Chapter 08's category and mandatory-error rules. An admitted unproved programmer obligation yields its configured ANOMALY. Required types, generic constraints, ABI matches, and explicit proof requirements **shall** be satisfied before acceptance. Suppression controls diagnostic emission; execution follows the bound contract.

#### 6.1 Core and selected capability conformance

The standard designation is **CPN26**, and the language name is **CPN26**. A Core conformance claim **shall** cover one root source unit, source edition and declaration binding, ordinary declarations and types, ordinary type/value generics, control flow, object lifetime and manual storage, configuration and diagnostics, and native object emission under its published core target. Its scalar operations **shall** implement the representations and policies required by that resolved core configuration. Source requirements **shall** be checked at their specified binding or execution boundary.

The Core root unit **shall** have an internal owner identity and the source/type/effect information needed to check that unit and its declared native boundaries. An implementation may represent those facts directly in compiler state. External manifests, JSON serialization, SHA-256 hashing, named module graphs, and persistent CPN26 interface artifacts are obligations of the selected capabilities below. A Core compiler can emit an ordinary native object and bind C or supported C++ declarations under its target contract; linking that object with foreign objects uses native symbol and ABI contracts.

| Optional capability | Selected operation and requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `compilation.modules` | Bind named modules, partitions, imports, exports, and their logical dependency graph. A joint compilation may obtain every declaration from the selected source inputs. |
| `compilation.separate` | Produce or consume independently compiled CPN26 interface material under a declared versioned protocol; requires `compilation.modules`. |
| `tooling.contract_export` | Produce the requested standard public records with Chapter 29's canonical JSON, references, and SHA-256 fingerprints. This capability is independent of module and separate-compilation support. |

Chapter 08 defines their disabled defaults. A requiring source construct or artifact request **shall** establish that its capability is available and enabled. Native linkage alone establishes a native boundary, while a separately compiled CPN26 semantic import selects `compilation.separate`. A provider's private interface protocol may realize separate compilation with `tooling.contract_export = false`; its identity, binding, compatibility, and collision-resolution checks **shall** still satisfy Chapter 11. An export request selects the public transport of already established semantic facts.

An implementation may claim any supported combination of the standard's optional capabilities. An optional claim **shall** implement the corresponding clauses for its published support set. Named modules, separate compilation, public contract export, high-accuracy numerics, extended formats, allocating numerical families, mathematical functions, advanced generics, reflection, language exceptions, standard-library modules, and managed concurrency have the capability boundaries defined by their owning chapters. Their presence in this standard defines the contract of a selected feature.

| Capability state | Required transition |
| --- | --- |
| Available | Publish the provider and the exact supported operations and contracts. |
| Enabled | Admit uses under the resolved configuration and expose applicable declarations. |
| Required by a program | Bind each used operation and its transitive dependencies, and supply their selected execution or compile-time support. |

Importing an optional catalogue **shall** expose its capability-gated declarations. A requiring use **shall** establish the needed claim before binding. An unsupported use yields the applicable capability diagnostic. Core conformance remains valid for programs within its declared core support. Capability closure **shall** follow actual semantic dependencies, including a selected operation's own supporting algorithms and resources.

#### 6.2 Numerical claims and resource contracts

An optional numerical claim **shall** identify the operation, format, admitted controls, delivery form, value/status contract, and resources defined by Chapters 05 and 18. Support for a representation, one function, or one delivery form **shall** establish that stated subset. The provider may share algorithms across entries and expose groups whose members have explicit contracts. Correctly rounded, component-exact, and approximate entries **shall** bind independently through their actual dependency sets.

A selected exact or correctly rounded entry **shall** deliver its promised result on success. Its provider **shall** choose an implementation and publish the resource and failure contract required by that interface. A mathematical reference formula specifies the result relation; physical algorithms, intermediate representations, and workspace follow the selected provider contract. Approximate results **shall** use a claimed approximation relation.

An implementation's conformance claim **shall** identify CPN26 as its source designation, its core target ABI and configuration, and its selected capability claims with provider identities and dependencies. A documented compiler/target description may supply this information for Core. A selected standard contract export **shall** use Chapter 29's identity and encoding rules. Internal semantic records and private interface protocols **shall** preserve the relevant identities and checks in their declared representation. Compilation budgets and optional analysis belong to the build context.

Portability applies to compatible operation contracts across targets. Explicit representations, exact/checked operations, strict/reproducible policies, versioned providers, and standard wire encodings establish stronger common contracts where requested. Native selection grants the implementation freedoms defined by its bound target contract.

<a id="chapter-22-static-reflection"></a>

## CPN26 Static Reflection Specification

### 1. Scope and normative model

Static reflection shall evaluate compiler-established descriptions of declarations, types, expressions, and admitted foreign entities. `std::meta::Info` is a compile-time value: it supports copying, canonical-identity comparison, consteval parameters/results, and compile-time temporary collections. Runtime materialization shall use the explicit descriptor operation in Section 12.

Reflection shall apply ordinary binding, access, completeness, and definition-site policy rules. Its query results describe semantic entities; runtime object access shall use the resulting ordinary operation's own lifetime and ownership contract. Reflection and declaration generation are independently selected capabilities under [Chapter 08](#chapter-08-runtime-configuration). Their execution phase follows the [core model](#chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance).

### 2. Intrinsic reflection syntax

The [core grammar](#chapter-15-grammar-binding) defines three nonoverloadable intrinsic forms: `reflect_type<T>`, `reflect_decl(name[, function_type])`, and `reflect_expr(expression)`.

`reflect_type<T>` describes type `T`; the type need not be complete for its nominal identity to be reflected. `reflect_decl(name)` describes the declaration denoted by its qualified-id in the current binding and accessibility environment. If a callable name denotes multiple overloads, the second argument is a function type that selects one exact declaration by its canonical parameter, return, receiver, and effect contract. The selector shall identify exactly one declaration; failure is ERROR.

`reflect_expr(e)` shall type-check e in an unevaluated context and return its static type, value category, unambiguous selected declaration, and declared effects. The expression shall satisfy its capability and accessibility requirements. Query evaluation contributes compile-time metadata events only.

Each intrinsic shall return Info under the surrounding definition-site configuration. A use within a runtime function shall consume the handle entirely during constant evaluation. For example:

```cpn
consteval usize count_members() {
    auto t(reflect_type<MyRecord>);
    return std::meta::direct_field_count(t);
}

constexpr usize member_count(count_members());
```

This example requires a complete, sealed `MyRecord` when `direct_field_count` is invoked. If it is incomplete at that point, the evaluator reports the corresponding required-constant error rather than returning an arbitrary count.

### 3. Metadata identity, kinds, and equality

An Info shall describe one semantic entity or expression descriptor. Standard `std::meta::Kind` cases are `Type`, `Variable`, `Function`, `Constructor`, `Destructor`, `Field`, `Base`, `Enumerator`, `UnionCase`, `Alias`, `Namespace`, `Module`, `GenericFamily`, `GenericParameter`, and `Expression`. A versioned provider may expose additional declared kinds. An inapplicable query shall produce its named compile-time MetaError Result or its terminating-query diagnostic.

Declaration identity shall use the owning module/package, declaration, selected specialization, and relevant representation contract. `reflect_type<Alias>` shall identify the underlying type; `reflect_decl(Alias)` shall identify the alias declaration. `underlying_type` obtains the aliased type from its declaration handle.

`same_entity(a,b)` shall compare canonical entity identities. Expression handles shall compare their bound semantic expression identity in the compilation context. Opaque handles support equality; `stable_key(info)` supplies the provider's deterministic logical grouping key. The key's portability and encoding are properties of its published provider version.

Canonical identities and member order shall derive from declared logical inputs. Physical paths, worker order, compiler addresses, and internal allocations are implementation data outside those identities.

### 4. Standard query surface

The standard `std::meta` module provides the following semantic operations. Names in this table are ordinary library-level entry points backed by the static-reflection provider. Their inputs and outputs are compile-time-only unless an output is an ordinary permitted constant scalar or string literal value.

| Query | Required semantics |
| --- | --- |
| `kind(info)` | Return the entity kind. |
| `same_entity(a,b)` | Compare canonical semantic identities. |
| `name(info)` | Return the source-level declared name, if present and accessible. |
| `qualified_name(info)` | Return the canonical CPN26 qualified name when the entity has one. |
| `owner(info)` | Return the declaring scope/module entity. |
| `type_of(info)` | Return the reflected type of a field, variable, function result where applicable, or expression. |
| `value_category(info)` | Return the static value category for an expression reflection only. |
| `is_complete(info)` | Return whether the described type is sealed and complete at this query point. |
| `is_const(info)` | Return the declared applicable top-level const qualification. |
| `is_public(info)` | Return whether the declaration is publicly accessible from the query environment. |
| `direct_fields(type_info)` | Return direct fields of a sealed type, excluding inherited fields, filtered for access. |
| `direct_field_count(type_info)` | Return the number of entries that direct_fields would expose, as usize; the same sealing and access requirements apply. An unrepresentable count is a required-constant error. |
| `authored_fields(type_info)` | Return the accessible original source-declared fields of a record, including in an unsealed generation owner. |
| `staged_fields(type_info)` | During its owning generation, return accessible authored fields followed by fields of prior committed generation batches; never return the pending batch. |
| `direct_bases(type_info)` | Return direct base descriptions, including their virtual/nonvirtual attributes. |
| `methods(type_info)` | Return accessible declared member functions with their canonical signatures. |
| `enumerators(enum_info)` | Return the declared enumerators and their exact typed values. |
| `union_cases(union_info)` | Return the declared tagged-union cases and payload declarations. |
| `parameters(function_info)` | Return ordered parameter descriptions. |
| `result_type(function_info)` | Return the declared function result type. |
| `effects(function_info)` | Return declared exception, async, ownership, borrowing, and lifetime-effect contracts. |
| `attributes(info)` | Return only registered, reflectable attributes permitted by this query context. |
| `type_size(type_info)` / `type_alignment(type_info)` | Query the complete type's target size and alignment. |
| `field_layout(field_info)` | Return an optional representable byte/bit-offset description under the target ABI provider. |

Query collections shall be immutable compile-time sequences. Direct collections contain the owner's direct declarations in declaration order, followed by generated declarations in commit order. An inherited-member traversal requires its separate path-identity contract, including virtual-base uniqueness. Query readiness shall follow the single staging table in [Chapter 23](#chapter-23-compile-time-generation).

Collection filtering shall use the query environment's access authority. Its length, positions, and returned identities shall describe exactly the accessible declarations.

### 5. Access control and privacy

Each query shall apply lexical visibility, module exports, private/protected access, and the owner-issued grant matrix in [Chapter 23, Section 5.1](#51-owner-authorized-member-access). A public caller receives public metadata; a matching meta_grant admits that record's authorized metadata to the named module.

```cpn
[[meta_grant(geometry.generators)]]
struct Point {
private:
    i32 internal_id(0);
};
```

The provider shall supply authorized private metadata through access-filtered interface material, including a separately sealed sidecar where applicable. Public serialization or re-export of that metadata shall require its own ordinary visibility authorization. A generated public accessor shall satisfy the distinct derive_access and signature rules in Chapter 23.

A required query with insufficient authority shall produce an access ERROR. A valid filtered enumeration may be empty; denied inspection is a failed query. The compiler shall retain that distinction during generic checking.

### 6. Completeness, layout, and class state

A forward declaration or type-only import shall provide its declared identity. Field traversal, size, completed traits, and layout-dependent observations shall require the corresponding completion stage and reachable interface contract. The query-stage table in Chapter 23 governs authored skeletons, active generation, and sealing.

For a sealed complete type, type_size and type_alignment shall use the same target profile as sizeof and alignof. field_layout shall return an offset only when the ABI establishes a stable representable offset. A dynamically adjusted subobject may instead use an explicitly admitted member-access operation.

Lifecycle metadata may describe Manual, Complete, virtual-base ownership, destructor/Cleanup effects, and selected special-operation contracts. It describes the declared protocol. A runtime access or transfer shall execute under Chapter 06's object-state and responsibility rules.

### 7. Reflection of expressions and operations

An operation-availability query shall check the declared generic domain and return its query-specific property result. `std::meta::try_*` distinguishes property inapplicability from malformed source, inaccessible declarations, and failed required evaluation under the standard query error contract. Generic candidate selection shall use Chapter 27's decision procedure.

`addressable_member(info)` shall describe whether an ordinary member-reference operation can designate the selected field. `get(object, field_info)` shall require a compile-time-known field handle and perform ordinary member access once, preserving qualification, category, borrow origin, access authority, and generation validity. Its runtime validation policy is the selected memory/lifecycle policy; the reflected handle supplies the member identity.

### 8. Generic interaction and specialization identity

A generic definition shall justify reflection queries through its declared constraints and reachable metadata. A public consteval function may accept Info and shall publish the metadata needed by its callers. Ordinary generic value arguments retain their admitted kinds from the type specification.

Reflection of a specialization shall return the already selected specialization identity and accessible members. An unapplied family's reflected surface shall contain its declaration, parameters, and constraints. An advanced-generic reflection capability may additionally expose Chapter 26's recursive kind tree, fixed and repeated parameter descriptors, captured partial arguments, and constructor mapping identity. A named constructor alias shall retain its declaration handle and its bound constructor identity as the corresponding query contracts specify.

An associated projection shall retain its full constraint application and selected explicit or structural witness identity. Structural evidence shall use the completed member and catalogue environment required by Chapters 26 and 27. Reflection shall observe that established selection at its admitted stage; the generation staging model determines when the relevant evidence is complete.

### 9. Constants, type information, and evaluation stages

Reflection shall execute under the target constant-evaluation rules in Chapter 10 and the query budgets in Chapter 08. Ordinary constant scalar or literal-string results may be materialized through their normal value contracts. Runtime owned text shall be constructed through its selected text/resource interface. Compiler metadata shall remain in its compile-time phase unless the program explicitly selects Section 12's runtime descriptor operation.

### 10. Representation queries and ABI promises

A foreign reflection provider shall expose the nominal, layout, and callable properties established by its selected ABI contract. An opaque foreign binding supplies only its admitted identity and operations. Generated foreign declarations shall satisfy the same verified ABI or explicit adapter requirements as authored declarations.

### 11. Reflection availability and configuration

Chapter 08 defines reflection capability keys, defaults, and evaluation budgets. The selected provider shall publish supported entity kinds, properties, layout capabilities, and metadata format revision. A required unavailable query shall fail at its use. Required-evaluation resource exhaustion shall retain its distinct compilation-resource outcome.

A compiled generic shall retain its definition-bound reflection requirements. Consumers shall supply those required providers and metadata or a declared compatible bridge.

### 12. Runtime descriptors are explicit

The separately selected `std.meta.runtime` operation shall materialize a descriptor from a sealed type and an explicit visibility/representation selection. The result shall be an ordinary immutable object or caller-owned serialized asset with a declared storage, version, access filter, image owner, allocator if needed, and unloading contract.

Exported descriptor content shall respect the materialization site's permitted export authority. Foreign descriptors shall describe operations under the corresponding foreign provider contract. Runtime invocation shall retain ordinary ABI, object lifetime, ownership, and failure requirements.

### 13. Diagnostics and conformance boundary cases

A conforming implementation shall distinguish unavailable capability, inaccessible property, incomplete type, property inapplicability, dependency cycle, and evaluation-budget exhaustion. Required query failures shall use the central diagnostic disposition and a stable logical location.

| Case | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Reflect a complete public record type | A valid compile-time type handle. |
| Reflect a forward-declared type | Valid identity; size and fields unavailable until complete. |
| Query `authored_fields` from a generator inside an unsealed record | Accessible authored field skeleton only, with stable source order. |
| Query `direct_fields` for that unsealed record | Incomplete/sealing `ERROR`; no speculative final field set. |
| Reflect a type alias | Underlying type identity; alias declaration separately reflectable. |
| Query direct fields outside a class with private fields | Only members reachable under current access rights. |
| Directly reflect an inaccessible private member from another module with no grant | Access `ERROR`; an authorized public-member enumeration remains visibility-filtered. |
| Inspect private authored fields under a valid owner-authored `meta_grant` | Metadata inspection is admitted; no runtime member-access permission follows. |
| Generate a private-member access using only `meta_grant` | Access ERROR unless independent ordinary access or the applicable `derive_access` supplies authority. |
| Use `derive_access` without permission to inspect the requested private metadata | The metadata query still fails with access ERROR. |
| Query `is_complete` for the currently executing derive target | False; the specialization has its unsealed identity. |
| Query `direct_fields` or final size of that derive target | Premature-observation ERROR under the required query stage. |
| Query an imported type-only declaration's layout | Completeness `ERROR`. |
| Inspect `reflect_expr(++x)` | No increment and no numeric status event; expression must still be well typed. |
| Query a virtual base's fixed offset where no fixed offset exists | NotRepresentable Result/error. |
| Reflect a closed tagged union | Case/payload declarations only; no runtime active-tag read. |
| Pass an Info handle to `extern "C"` | `ERROR`: compile-time-only type has no ABI transport. |
| Store an Info handle in a runtime object | `ERROR` independent of object size. |
| Reflect a generated declaration from its own incomplete generation | Generation-cycle or premature observation `ERROR`. |
| Use a foreign type with no layout descriptor | Opaque reflection only. |
| Request an unavailable provider in an enabled query | Capability `ERROR`, not guessed metadata. |

A Reflection capability claim shall cover the enabled query surface and its access, identity, staging, and error contracts.
