<a id="chapter-23-compile-time-generation"></a>

## CPN26 Compile-Time Metaprogramming and Declaration Generation Specification

### 1. Purpose and separation of concerns

Declaration generation shall evaluate typed syntax in the compile-time phase and commit validated declarations into an authorized lexical scope. Each emitted declaration shall undergo the grammar, binding, type, access, effect, lifecycle, configuration, and ABI checks applicable to an authored declaration at that insertion point. The [core execution model](#chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance) governs its subsequent runtime behavior.

This chapter owns generation staging, transactions, hygiene, and the permission matrix shared with [static reflection](#chapter-22-static-reflection). Chapter 08 owns capability/default/budget selection.

### 2. Generation blocks and enabled scopes

Chapter 15 owns the generation and quotation grammar. A generation declaration shall use `generate { ... }`, with explicit `emit(expression);` submissions.

A generation body shall admit if, if constexpr, for, while, do, nested compounds, local declarations, and expressions eligible for required evaluation. Break and continue shall target a loop in that body. Each helper invocation shall satisfy the same required-evaluation environment and may return its admitted compile-time value. The admitted statement set shall retain transaction completion in the containing generation body.

A generate declaration shall occupy the file scope of a Core root unit or selected named-module unit, namespace scope, or the body of a directly owned struct or class. Its emitted declarations shall belong to that exact lexical scope. The owning compilation scope shall be the Core root owner or named module established by Chapter 11. Every submitted declaration shall satisfy the scope and ownership validation in Section 7.

Emit shall occur inside a generate body and accept one std::meta::Declaration or immutable ordered Declarations sequence. It shall evaluate the argument once and append the candidates to that body's pending transaction. Publication shall occur through Section 7's atomic commit.

A consteval helper shall return candidate declarations to its caller. The enclosing generate body shall own the transaction and explicitly submit those values with emit.

### 3. Generation values and syntax quotations

The compile-time `std::meta` generation facility supplies:

| Type or operation | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `std::meta::Name` | A compiler-validated identifier, not a raw source fragment. |
| `std::meta::Declaration` | One parsed, typed declaration-syntax candidate. |
| `std::meta::Declarations` | An immutable ordered sequence of declaration candidates. |
| `std::meta::SyntaxExpr` | A parsed expression-syntax candidate, not an evaluated runtime value. |
| `std::meta::identifier(text)` | Construct a target-scope declaration identifier from an NFC-valid source identifier spelling. |
| `std::meta::data_member(name, type_info, access)` | Construct one ordinary stored field declaration for a record target. |
| `std::meta::static_member(name, type_info, initializer, access)` | Construct one static member declaration with an explicit initialization contract. |
| `std::meta::declarations(elements...)` | Construct an ordered sequence from declaration candidates. |

These types shall belong to the compile-time phase. A versioned provider may add typed constructors for further declaration kinds by publishing their complete syntax-tree and semantic contracts. Every requested constructor shall have its required capability.

A quotation shall use Chapter 15's `quote declaration { ... }` or `quote expression { ... }` form and produce typed syntax parsed at its definition site. It shall contain the selected declaration or expression category. Its splices shall have the following inputs:

| Splice form | Required compile-time input and position |
| --- | --- |
| `splice_type(expression)` | A reflected type at a type position. |
| `splice_name(expression)` | A validated Name at an admitted identifier position. |
| `splice_expr(expression)` | Correctly typed expression or constant syntax at an expression position. |

The checker shall validate each splice before emission and preserve its grammatical category.

Quotation identifiers shall carry Section 8's definition-bound, quotation-local, or target-introduced provenance. A committed declaration head shall enter the target scope. `std::meta::fresh_name()` shall produce a helper identity stable for the same canonical inputs and emission ordinal; its physical spelling may remain private.

Example, with the generation capability enabled and the standard meta module imported:

```cpn
export module geometry;
import std.meta;

generate {
    emit(quote declaration {
        i32 doubled(i32 value) { return value + value; }
    });
}

struct Header {
    u32 length(0);
    generate {
        emit(std::meta::data_member(
            std::meta::identifier("checksum"),
            reflect_type<u32>,
            std::meta::Access::Private));
    }
};
```

With meta.generate, meta.generate_layout, and the required std.meta provider enabled, doubled shall become an owning-module function and checksum an ordinary field in Header's generated-member segment. Their subsequent execution, arithmetic, initialization, layout, and access shall use the selected ordinary contracts.

### 4. Generated declarations and lexical lookup

Section 6 shall establish the authored skeleton and generated transaction sequence. The skeleton shall retain every authored field's declaration order, allowing authorized skeleton queries throughout the record independently of the generation block's physical position.

Authored stored fields shall retain their order. Generated fields shall follow them in successful-transaction order; methods, aliases, and statics shall preserve that layout order and the base order. A generated constructor or destructor shall enter before sealing and satisfy the ordinary overload, special-operation, and responsibility rules. Existing declarations shall retain their identities and collision rules.

File-scope and namespace emissions shall enter at the generation declaration's logical source position. Earlier nondependent bindings shall retain their candidate sets. Normal declaration-before-use and forward declarations shall remain available. A sealed record shall expose its complete final member index under Chapter 10's binding rule.

A generated declaration shall use its target's owning compilation identity and generation-site configuration. Its generator function shall execute under its own captured definition contract; the returned declaration shall be checked under the target's source, ABI, and lifetime contract while preserving hygienic external bindings. The target configuration shall remain fixed throughout the transaction.

### 5. Derivation attributes

A record may explicitly request generation from a named function through the standard `derive` attribute:

```cpn
[[derive(geometry::generators::emit_comparisons)]]
struct Coordinate {
    i32 x(0);
    i32 y(0);
};
```

A derive argument shall resolve to one reachable exported consteval function or fully applied specialization with the exact conceptual signature `std::meta::Declarations Generator(std::meta::Info target)`. Section 6 shall schedule that invocation after specialization and skeleton binding, and commit its returned declarations in sequence order.

A derivation transaction shall be identified by selected target specialization, selected generator, zero-based ordinal among that definition's derive attributes, and captured definition environment. Generic attribute references shall be checked at definition; derivation shall execute for each selected concrete specialization. Equivalent separate compilations shall reproduce the same canonical declarations and transaction identity.

A derivation may add functions, nonstorage aliases, constraints, and static declarations under their ordinary contracts. Representation-changing declarations shall require an in-record generate block and meta.generate_layout. Existing user lifecycle declarations shall retain their identities; additional lifecycle declarations shall satisfy ordinary overload rules.

Each derivation shall receive the access-filtered metadata and submitted-member authority established by Section 5.1. Emitted references shall retain their hygiene provenance, and signatures shall satisfy the target's ordinary visibility and ABI contracts.

Derivations shall execute in source attribute order. Repeating a canonical generator on one record shall require its published repeatable contract. Dependency cycles shall fail the required-evaluation check in Section 6.

#### 5.1 Owner-authorized member access

The following table is the canonical authorization contract for reflection and derivation grants:

| Owner-authored attribute on record R | Canonical subject | Granted operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `meta_grant(M)` | Current owning module or reachable imported module M | Inspect R's otherwise available nonpublic metadata in M's query environment. |
| `derive_access(G)` | One generator selected under derive's signature rule | Form and execute ordinary R-member accesses in member definitions submitted by G's matching derive transactions on R. |

R's owning compilation scope shall author each grant on R's definition and identify that author through its canonical owner identity. Each attribute's subject shall resolve under its schema in the table; meta_grant(M) shall retain its named-module subject. All attribute references shall be resolved before derivation begins, so textual placement of a grant among attributes preserves the same authority. Duplicate grants to the same canonical subject shall be rejected. A valid unused grant shall remain compile-time authority.

Each grant shall apply to R's own declarations under ordinary member-access rules. Private declarations of bases and unrelated records require their separate authority. Inspection authority belongs to the named module; helper calls into another module shall use that helper's authority. Submitted-member authority belongs to the matching target/generator transaction, including its repeatable derive ordinals. Ordinary generator calls, other targets, and unrelated generate blocks shall use their ordinary lexical authority.

A generic definition shall capture its grants for the selected instances derived from that definition. Separately authored specializations, derived records, and nested records shall establish their own grants. The compiler shall reject generated attempts to author, modify, or re-export a grant.

A generator requiring private metadata and private-member references shall supply both applicable authorities, whether from the table or independently valid lexical access. Syntax and Info values carry identity/provenance; the validating transaction supplies authority. Member access shall preserve qualification, overload, active-case, generation, construction state, ownership, and effect requirements.

Submitted members shall retain their declared access. An authorized public member may return a permitted value computed from R's private field. Its signature and exported metadata shall independently satisfy ordinary public visibility. Authorized definition material may include private identities needed to check its body; public reflection shall still use its own access filter.

The semantic interface shall record target identity, subject owner or generator/definition identity, grant kind, and applicable derive ordinals. Validation shall establish the exact matching grant before accepting a private reference. Grant or generator-contract changes shall invalidate dependent generated definitions. Chapter 21 shall govern internal identity and selected external publication of these records.

```cpn
import schema.generators;

[[meta_grant(schema.generators)]]
[[derive(schema::generators::emit_read_id)]]
[[derive_access(schema::generators::emit_read_id)]]
class Entry {
    i32 internal_id(0);
};
```

Here meta_grant admits field inspection and derive_access admits the submitted member body's field access. Removing either authority leaves that corresponding operation subject to ordinary access checking. Every generated access shall satisfy the field's runtime lifetime requirement.

#### 5.2 Conformance catalogue publication

Ordinary aliases, generic declarations, and constraints may be emitted through admitted typed-syntax constructors. A public `satisfy` conformance shall originate in an authored declaration of its owning compilation scope and satisfy Chapter 26's ownership rules. The generation validator shall reject a submitted conformance declaration.

An authored conformance may use generated methods after their required declaration and completion checks succeed. A committed generated alias, constant, constructor family, or ordinary method may supply structural evidence under Chapter 26. Structural witness formation shall use the sealed subject and completed bound catalogue required by Chapter 27. Witness publication shall record the selected evidence and its canonical identities after these dependencies complete.

### 6. Staging, sealing, and determinism

The semantic stages for an owning compilation scope and a record are:

1. Resolve the Core root or named-module identity, any selected imports, configuration, canonical authored declarations, and their access permissions.
2. Build authored record skeletons and dependency edges without demanding complete generated layouts.
3. Process derive attributes in deterministic declaration order. For each attribute, evaluate its function, validate its pending batch, and commit that batch atomically before beginning the next derivation; a failed transaction commits nothing.
4. Process explicit generation bodies in the owning record's source order with the same evaluate, validate, and atomic-commit protocol. Each body sees prior committed derivations and generation batches, never its own pending output.
5. Seal the record/member index and resolve layout-dependent queries, special operations, overload sets, and generic constraints that depend on the final declaration set.
6. Establish exported interface metadata, canonical instantiation identity, native ABI declarations, and static initialization descriptors.

File-scope and namespace generation shall follow source order after their required source binding and any selected import resolution. A generated nested record shall enter the same staged sequence under a well-founded dependency. The owning source identity, tokenization profile, and any resolved imports shall remain fixed during generation.

The query-stage table is authoritative for both reflection and generation:

| Observed entity/stage | Available information |
| --- | --- |
| Incomplete nominal identity | Declared identity and reachable declaration properties. |
| Current authored record skeleton | Accessible authored declarations; authored_fields returns their field subset. |
| Active owning derivation/generation | Authored skeleton plus earlier committed batches through staged_fields; is_complete is false. |
| Current pending batch | Transaction-local syntax under validation; reflected publication begins at commit. |
| Sealed complete record | Final direct_fields, layout, completed overload/trait information, and is_complete true. |
| Unrelated sealed record during generation | Its ordinary complete query surface under the query's access rights. |

The active owning-generation context includes its selected derive function and permitted synchronous constant-evaluation helpers. It supplies stage information; Section 5.1 supplies access authority. A query requiring a later stage shall fail with the required dependency diagnostic. Each derivation shall execute once in its defined semantic order and observe that snapshot; later generation shall preserve earlier completed transactions.

The validator shall check grammar, identity, access provenance, and independently resolvable signatures before batch commit. Completion-dependent body binding, defaulted operations, and layout checks may remain pending until sealing. Their results become available at that completion stage. A sealing failure shall invalidate the enclosing record; publication requires all completion checks to succeed.

The compiler shall detect active dependency cycles across queries, generation, instantiation, and required evaluation. A cycle shall produce a required-evaluation error. Parallel evaluation shall produce the declarations and commit order prescribed by the serial semantics.

### 7. Emission validation and atomic commit

Before a batch is committed, the compiler validates all emitted nodes as though they were written at their logical insertion points, preserving the ordinary completion-dependent checks identified in Section 6. This includes the requirements that are decidable at that declaration phase:

- grammar and identifier validity, source normalization, reserved names, and case-sensitive collisions;
- supported declaration kind and allowed target scope;
- permitted effect attributes and ownership annotations;
- complete type and applicable generic requirements;
- legal initialization, constructor/delegation, destructor/Cleanup and virtual-base responsibility behavior;
- ordinary overload uniqueness, external symbol identity, linkage conventions, and public interface consistency;
- format/width capability availability, numeric-policy binding, and target ABI legality;
- accessibility and hygiene provenance, including attempted nonpublic disclosure;
- static-object declaration identity, explicit initialization dependencies, and deterministic source order.

A transaction shall publish its entire validated batch or publish nothing. Earlier independent committed batches retain their semantic results subject to ordinary whole-unit publication. Generation failure shall remain a compilation failure under the selected declaration contract.

`emit` shall submit compile-time syntax to its active transaction. The evaluator shall count declarations at successful batch validation. Exceeding a generation budget shall fail the current transaction with its compilation-resource diagnostic.

### 8. Hygiene, capture, and private-member contracts

Every syntax identifier shall carry exactly one provenance category. A definition-bound name shall resolve in its captured generator environment. A quotation-local name shall bind inside the generated syntax scope. A target-introduced name shall use its validated Name in the target scope and satisfy ordinary collision checks. Each binding shall retain its selected declaration and policy context.

A generator using a target-site name shall receive an explicit reflected declaration or validated Name with the corresponding binding authority. splice_expr shall preserve already bound declarations and effects. Generated lifecycle operations shall satisfy Chapter 06, and their runtime validation shall follow the target operation's selected policy.

The validator shall establish Section 5.1's authority independently of hygiene provenance. A definition-bound reference shall keep its actual selected declaration. An owner-authored generate block has its ordinary lexical access; external helpers execute under their own access environment. A lower-level syntax provider shall publish its mapping to the three provenance categories.

### 9. Cross-module generation and exports

A generated declaration shall belong to its target module and use that scope's explicit export context. Export validation shall establish public signature visibility, eligible interface-unit placement, and unique nominal identity.

An exported generator shall publish its versioned definition, query capabilities, required reflection material, and syntax-builder dependencies. A consumer may invoke it at an eligible scope owned by that consumer; compiled dependency declarations shall retain their original owner and generation transactions.

A generated field shall enter the owning type's ABI contract. Generated functions, constraints, and attributes shall enter their corresponding semantic interface identities. A selected standard contract export shall project these identities through Chapter 29. Dependency invalidation shall follow every exposed or transitively required definition change, while unrelated private helpers shall retain their independent identity.

An imported generic containing generation shall retain its defining module's policies, generator versions, target scope, and canonical specialization arguments. Grants shall remain those captured under Section 5.1. Repeated imports shall share the resulting canonical symbol and static-object identities under the ordinary instantiation rules.

### 10. Static objects, native code, and C/C++ interoperation

A generated static shall participate in the ordinary initialization, cancellation, commitment, and destruction graph. Its stable identity shall include the owning Core root or named module, generator invocation, target scope, and ordered emission ordinal. Generated native symbols and foreign bindings shall satisfy their selected function, ABI, and adapter contracts.

Runtime output shall contain emitted program entities and explicitly requested runtime descriptors. Compile-time syntax and reflection material remain in their defined phase under Chapter 21.

### 11. Compile-time effects and resource governance

Generation shall execute admitted required-constant operations and declaration transactions. Compiler-local workspace shall use the declared compilation budgets. Its input set shall consist of declared source/module/provider material and any explicitly supplied content-addressed extension inputs. The evaluator shall derive output solely from that set and the bound semantic configuration.

Chapter 08 defines generation capability keys, defaults, and limits. Reflection-dependent operations shall require meta.reflection; a provider may declare quotation-only generation with reflection disabled. Representation-changing emission shall require meta.generate_layout.

Required-evaluation budget exhaustion and dependency cycles shall fail the transaction. Query-specific try operations may return their defined property-inapplicability Results. These outcomes shall retain their distinct meanings in generic candidate selection.

### 12. Error classes, attribution, and reproducibility

A generated diagnostic shall identify the logical declaration, emission site, and originating generator or quotation. Its source mapping shall preserve those validated identities. Diagnostic presentation shall use the consumer's access rights when rendering private source content.

A conforming implementation shall distinguish at least:

| Diagnostic class | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `META001` | Reflection or generation capability disabled/unavailable. |
| `META002` | Metadata access forbidden by visibility/grant contract. |
| `META003` | Property requires a sealed/complete type or interface. |
| `META004` | Quotation, splice, or emitted declaration has invalid kind or type. |
| `META005` | Duplicate name, incompatible overload, or conflicting emitted entity. |
| `META006` | Generated declaration would change a forbidden owner, scope, ABI, or lifecycle contract. |
| `META007` | Reflection/generation dependency cycle. |
| `META008` | Required evaluation resource budget exhausted. |
| `META009` | Nondeterministic or undeclared external input requested. |
| `META010` | Invalid metadata identity, value/category, or hygiene provenance. |

Required generation failure shall use the central ERROR disposition. Optional analysis of an admitted metadata obligation shall use its configured diagnostic. These dispositions shall preserve the distinction between valid emitted syntax and failed required generation.

For equal canonical source, logical owner environment, target ABI, admitted inputs, generator definitions, and effective semantic configuration, implementations shall produce equal emitted declarations and logical order. The logical environment shall be the Core root or selected module map. Machine instruction selection and physical encoding shall follow the chosen implementation and target contract.

### 13. Normative boundary cases

| Case | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| `generate` at file scope in a Core root or named-module unit, or in an owned namespace | May add ordinary eligible declarations to that exact lexical scope. |
| `generate` inside a runtime function | ERROR: the declaration requires an admitted compile-time scope. |
| `emit` called from a normal `consteval` helper, with no enclosing generation block | `ERROR`; the helper may instead return a declaration value. |
| A failed batch emits two declarations, one invalid | Neither declaration from that batch is committed. |
| A field is emitted in a record with `meta.generate_layout = false` | `ERROR` even when `meta.generate = true`. |
| A `derive` function tries to add a stored instance field | `ERROR`; `derive` is nonstorage. |
| A generated function attempts private member access without access permission | `ERROR` despite its resulting class membership. |
| A foreign generator inspects a private field with meta_grant but has no applicable derive_access | Inspection may succeed; a submitted member body gains no private access from that fact. |
| An applicable owner-authored derive_access permits a submitted member body to read the target's private field | Ordinary member access is admitted, subject to qualification, lifetime, effects, and valid public signature rules. |
| A generator tries to emit meta_grant or derive_access | ERROR: these attributes require an authored owner grant. |
| A derive function queries authored_fields for its current unsealed target | Accessible authored fields, independent of the attribute's position in the record definition. |
| A later explicit generate block adds a field after derive completed | The field is appended by its transaction; the completed derive retains its committed output. |
| An emitted member body fails when the final owner index is sealed | The enclosing record fails completion and publication. |
| Generator uses `splice_type` in expression/name position | `ERROR`; splice categories are distinct. |
| A generated name duplicates an existing incompatible authored name | ERROR under ordinary collision validation. |
| Generator queries final layout of its own unsealed record | Dependency `ERROR`, not speculative layout. |
| Two generations commit independent methods under different worker scheduling | Same canonical identities and logical order. |
| Generator imports an undeclared new module | `ERROR`; module imports are frozen before generation. |
| Generation emits a C++ class with no verified target ABI | No direct C++ class ABI claim; explicit wrapper or provider contract required. |
| A generator returns a private metadata handle as a runtime value | `ERROR`; no representation or privilege escape. |
| A generated static object is initialized | Applies normal static logical ordering and destruction responsibility. |
| Generation is disabled while ordinary `consteval` is enabled | `consteval` remains available; emit/generation forms are unavailable. |

### 14. Standard library and conformance boundary

An implementation shall report Reflection, Declaration Generation, and Layout Generation as separate capabilities. Their claims shall respectively cover Chapter 22's query surface; this chapter's typed syntax, transactions, hygiene, and ordering; and generated layout with its ordinary lifecycle validation. The declared std.meta provider shall publish the supported surface. Explicit runtime descriptor materialization shall use std.meta.runtime and its ordinary object/resource contract.

<a id="chapter-24-contracts-effects"></a>

## CPN26 Contracts and Effect Signatures Specification

### 1. Scope and normative terminology

A callable contract shall describe three independent components: value/state requirements at defined boundaries, an effect upper bound for each callable phase, and lifetime/ownership transitions. This chapter owns the predicate rules, effect vocabulary, and validation modes. [Chapter 25](#chapter-25-effect-composition-boundaries) defines their composition across calls, tasks, ownership transfers, and foreign boundaries.

An effect denotes a possible action under the selected [abstract-machine observation contract](#chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance). Result alternatives are ordinary values. Failure effects shall use the selected outlet in Chapter 28; numerical operations shall use Chapter 04's resolved profile. Descriptors are static interface material; a runtime check exists when its selected contract requires evaluation.

### 2. Contract and effect syntax

Standard contract declarations use ordinary leading or permitted trailing attribute lists. The schema of these attributes is normative rather than an arbitrary user-defined expression macro:

```ebnf
contract-attribute = "requires", "(", contract-expression, ")"
                   | "ensures", "(", contract-expression, ")"
                   | "invariant", "(", contract-expression, ")"
                   | "effects", "(", effect-bound, ")"
                   | "admission_effects", "(", effect-bound, ")"
                   | "retains", "(", parameter-name, ",", owner-name, ")";
owner-name = parameter-name | "return_value";
effect-bound = "none" | effect-item, { ",", effect-item };
effect-item = "read", "(", effect-region, ")"
            | "write", "(", effect-region, ")"
            | "allocate", "(", effect-domain, ")"
            | "deallocate", "(", effect-domain, ")"
            | "volatile" | "atomic" | "synchronize" | "io"
            | "block" | "spawn" | "suspend" | "cancel_point"
            | "throw" | "trap", "(", trap-kind, ")"
            | "fp_status" | "fp_control"
            | "whole" | "foreign";
effect-region = "any" | "global" | parameter-name | "this";
effect-domain = "any" | parameter-name | "global";
trap-kind = "numeric" | "contract" | "any";
contract-expression = ? a well-typed Boolean expression with only admitted read effects
                        obeying the restrictions of Section 4 ?;
```

The parser shall interpret attribute payloads using their registered schemas. Attribute-schema words retain their ordinary lexical status outside that schema. Payload binding is a declaration-time operation. For example:

```cpn
[[requires(divisor != 0), ensures(return_value >= 0)]]
[[effects(read(data), trap(numeric))]]
declare i32 magnitude(const<i32>& data, i32 divisor);

[[effects(none)]]
declare u32 encode_tag(u8 code) noexcept;
```

The standard effects schema shall retain its registered identity. Parameter names in effects shall resolve to canonical parameter positions for signature identity; overload identity follows the type specification.

A record-level `[[invariant(expression)]]` shall apply to a complete native class, struct, or tagged union. A foreign adapter supplying an invariant shall establish its representation and synchronization contract. The record and all reflected/generated contributions shall retain their owning-module and bound-configuration requirements.

An attribute requires shall state a value precondition. A generic requires clause shall determine compile-time candidate eligibility under Chapter 27. Each shall be checked in its own phase.

### 3. Effective effect signatures and open-world defaults

For each callable phase, `[[effects(S)]]` shall bound every externally observable effect that phase may perform, including selected calls and required completion. A missing bound is open under the selected capabilities. An opaque call shall contribute its declared bound, or the conservative open bound when no narrower contract is available.

`effects(none)` is the empty bound. Computation on independent local values and inert local cleanup may satisfy it. Access through an input pointer/reference contributes its specified region effect. Caller-side argument evaluation and parameter admission retain their own phase attribution in Chapter 25.

`noexcept` shall exclude language-exception propagation across its phase boundary. Internal handled exceptions retain their ordinary effects. Other terminal outlets, Result values, cancellation, Whole, allocation, blocking, and divergence shall be governed by their own effect categories. A simultaneous noexcept and escaping-throw declaration is contradictory. Termination and progress promises require their own contract, including never's normal-return rule.

#### 3.1 Effect categories

| Category | Governed observable behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `read(p)` | Read through the region reachable from argument `p` or the receiver `this`, excluding independent local copies. |
| `write(p)` | Modify the region reachable from p or this under its separate authority and synchronization obligations. |
| `read(global)`, `write(global)` | Read/write externally observable global or static state. |
| `read(any)`, `write(any)` | Respective access to any permitted region, including opaque indirect accesses. |
| `allocate(d)`, `deallocate(d)` | Acquire/release storage or persistent allocation accounting in resource domain `d` or `any`; attempted admission that fails without a durable allocation is still a possible allocation effect. |
| `volatile` | Perform a volatile access or provider operation with comparable volatile visibility. |
| `atomic` | Perform atomic access under the selected memory order; synchronization edges follow that order's contract. |
| `synchronize` | Create or participate in lock, fence, wait/notify, release/acquire, or equivalent synchronization actions. |
| `io` | Produce or consume externally observable device, file, network, console, or process/environment I/O. |
| `block` | Potentially stop progress awaiting an external event or other execution agent; this is distinct from suspending a CPN26 coroutine. |
| `spawn` | Initiate a new independent execution agent or schedule owned work. |
| `suspend` | Suspend the current async execution frame and resume through its continuation protocol. |
| `cancel_point` | Accept a cancellation request and transfer along the defined cooperative cancellation exit. |
| `throw` | Allow a language exception to cross this callable phase's exit boundary. |
| `trap(numeric)`, `trap(contract)` | Admit the corresponding terminal outlet. `trap(any)` admits the standardized synchronous nonreturning failure outlets, including mandatory local exception-boundary termination. |
| `fp_status` | Read or update floating status observed under the selected numerical contract. |
| `fp_control` | Read/change observed FP controls or perform a context switch that changes those observed controls. |
| `whole` | Invoke the permitted destructor-coordinator Whole control transfer. |
| `foreign` | Enter a foreign execution boundary with effects not fully represented by native regions, or with a separately declared foreign provider effect contract. |

`read(p)` shall cover the region reachable through p under its declared bounds. A published exact-subregion descriptor may narrow that region when its evidence and schema are available. Pointer validity, alignment, aliasing, provenance, and lifetime remain the corresponding memory obligations; effect regions may overlap.

A write(p) bound shall include the reads of the same value needed to compute that write when those reads have no independent observable effect. An independently observable read shall require read(p). A declaration may list both bounds explicitly.

An atomic operation shall additionally carry synchronize when its selected order participates in inter-agent synchronization. Volatile, atomic, and synchronization obligations shall each follow Chapter 13. I/O shall additionally carry block when it may wait for an external event.

A foreign call shall use its published effect contract. A verified adapter may expose a fully translated native bound when it accounts for all observable behavior and ABI requirements. An opaque foreign call shall retain its conservative foreign bound.

#### 3.2 Cleanup and completion effects

A phase bound shall include its return construction, temporary/local/parameter retirement, Cleanup, permitted rollback, resource transitions, and selected calls. Chapter 25 assigns these operations to their caller, admission, execution, and completion phases.

An explicitly checked value operation may contribute trap(numeric); its corresponding Result operation contributes the effects of its value computation, status delivery, and resource work. Each replaces only its own specified failure outlet. Native numerical operations shall use their provider-declared value/fault/environment contract. A selected ContractTrap boundary shall contribute trap(contract). These contributions shall reflect the resolved operation rather than a presumed universal arithmetic mode.

### 4. Preconditions and postconditions

`[[requires(P)]]` shall state a condition at completed parameter admission before body entry. Its variables refer to admitted parameters and an eligible live receiver. An exported condition is a caller obligation and, in check mode, an entry predicate. Argument expressions and parameter construction occur once under the call contract.

`[[ensures(Q)]]` shall state a condition at Chapter 25's prepared normal-return boundary: after result construction and body-local cleanup, while parameters remain live, and before their retirement and final publication. A nonnormal path uses its selected failure/control outlet. Passing ensures establishes that check only; later retirement and completion retain their own failure behavior.

`return_value` shall designate the single constructed result, or the admitted referent of a reference result, through a read-only view. It is available for non-void ensures clauses. Named parameters shall expose their current values, including moved-from states. Returned borrows shall cover the caller's admitted use after publication. A returned Result, including Err, shall satisfy applicable ensures through valid active-case access.

A predicate shall have bool type and a closed admitted evaluation contract: reads of valid live regions and value computations that allocate nothing, propagate no language exception, cause no terminal transfer, suspend no task, block no agent, and produce no observable state/status mutation. Observer calls shall have a compatible closed bound and established nonfailing nested checks. FP predicates shall select nonraising comparison or representation/classification operations. Their required providers shall be available at declaration binding.

Raw or shared designations in a predicate shall carry the appropriate lifetime and synchronization obligation. A proved invalid designation is invalid source; an admitted but unproved ordinary obligation shall use the central ANOMALY policy. Document mode shall retain that obligation without executing the predicate. Prove mode shall establish its required evidence; check mode shall evaluate only under its valid access contract. Volatile, atomic-status, mutation, and exception-aggregate observations lie outside this pure predicate domain.

A selected check whose predicate is false shall enter ContractTrap. A required constant evaluation shall apply its corresponding success rule. The optimizer may use a predicate as an assumption when proved, established by a dominating check, or selected under the explicit trusted contract in Section 6. An unchecked documented requirement remains a programmer obligation.

#### 4.1 Completion values and explicit snapshots

An ensures expression shall read values accessible at its completion boundary. A before/after comparison shall carry its prior value through an explicitly constructed argument, object, or operation-specific result. Those values shall use their ordinary construction, resource, and lifetime contracts.

#### 4.2 Multiple conditions and failure order

Checks shall evaluate clauses in declaration order, preserving source order within an attribute list and ordinary Boolean short-circuiting. Each reached clause shall execute once. The first false clause shall select the failure boundary. Elimination of a proved-true clause shall preserve the observations selected by the check policy.

A check diagnostic shall identify the stable declaration and clause ordinal. A policy omitting execution shall report only established analysis facts. Invalid memory access during an admitted predicate execution shall follow its memory-failure contract.

### 5. Record invariants and lifecycle boundaries

A record invariant shall describe a complete Alive object at its stable exposure boundaries. Under a checking policy, it shall be evaluated after complete construction, at entry to eligible public Alive-receiver operations, and at the normal-return exposure of eligible public mutating operations. A base invariant shall apply at the corresponding live base boundary. Construction and destruction phases shall use Chapter 06's own state contracts.

An external mutable alias shall retain its memory and synchronization obligations between boundaries. Optimizer reliance shall use Section 6's proof/check/trust rule. A representation constructor or foreign adapter shall establish the invariant before publishing a conforming native record. A raw representation operation that changes the property shall leave restoration to the programmer before subsequent invariant-governed exposure. Optional invariant validation shall follow its selected policy.

### 6. Contract validation and configuration

Chapter 08 supplies the sole key/domain/default table. The owning declaration shall bind its validation policy and publish that policy with its contract. An importer shall use that bound contract.

| Validation mode | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| check | Evaluate reached predicates and select ContractTrap on a false result. Attribute their admitted reads and possible terminal outcome as boundary-check effects. |
| prove | Establish every required reachable entry/normal-return condition; failure to establish required evidence is a compilation failure. |
| document | Preserve the stated obligation and applicable analysis diagnostic. Execution and optimizer assumptions require their separate authority. |
| trusted | With contracts.trusted_assumptions selected, permit compiler reliance on the stated condition under the author's explicit correctness obligation. |

An unmet trusted promise falls outside that explicitly selected optimization contract's guarantees. Disabling optional value-contract checking shall preserve the source declarations needed for type, generic, and ABI compatibility. Ordinary language lifetimes and explicitly selected operation checks remain their own functional contracts.

Effect inference shall use the mode resolved by Chapter 08. Local mode shall inspect the current CFG and bound declaration/interface summaries. Interprocedural mode may additionally analyze available callee bodies to a conservative fixed point. Both shall preserve the distinction between a declared obligation, established evidence, and unknown implementation behavior. Release defaults to local mode; whole-program proof is an optional analysis strategy. Explicit proof and generic requirements shall retain their own acceptance rules.

### 7. Callable identity, redeclarations, and override compatibility

A callable signature shall retain its ordinary types, receiver, async admission shape, linkage/ABI, nonthrowing guarantee, normalized lifetime/ownership contracts, and effect bound. Address taking, indirect calls, generic witnesses, and virtual dispatch shall preserve that contract. Declarations differing only in effects shall redeclare the same ordinary overload and require compatible canonical contracts.

Chapter 25 shall define callable-bound substitution, phase-specific compatibility, and foreign adapters. An override shall admit every state permitted by its base precondition and establish at least the base postcondition on successful return. Stronger internal checks shall therefore preserve all valid base-contract calls.

A foreign ABI descriptor shall distinguish semantic contract fields from physical calling representation. Verified local wrappers may strengthen a foreign entry's exposed checks while preserving a consistent underlying symbol contract.

### 8. Generic constraints and effect queries

A generic effect requirement may depend on its declared callable witness and enabled compile-time metadata. The optional std.effects surface and query identities shall have their single definition in Chapter 25.

The definition shall bind its required effects, and Chapter 27 shall establish them for each selected witness. A closed declared contract supplies its published evidence; an open bound remains conservative. A generic returning a callable shall preserve that callable's selected type and captured policies. Changes affecting canonical effects shall enter instance identity and interface compatibility.

#### 8.1 Associated callable witnesses

An associated operation witness shall preserve the receiver, return category, nonthrowing, borrowing, retention, consumption, phase effects, and ABI contracts specified in Chapter 26. Chapter 27's proof procedure shall establish its relationship to the required bound, using immutable declaration-site contracts.

### 9. Diagnostics and soundness of optimization

The checker shall classify facts using the following semantic outcomes. Chapter 08 determines their diagnostic categories, filtering, and promotion.

| Fact | Semantic outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Malformed schema, contradictory contract, proved bound violation, or inadmissible phase | Invalid declaration or use. |
| Ordinary opaque call or external lifetime obligation remains unproved | Admitted programmer obligation; retain its ANOMALY disposition and conservative implementation knowledge. |
| Explicit prove requirement or required generic evidence is missing | Required proof/constraint failure. |
| Checked runtime predicate is false | ContractTrap. |
| Required constant contract evaluation fails | Required-evaluation failure. |
| A precise valid implementation summary is established | Evidence available for permitted optimization and diagnostics. |

An inferred implementation summary shall refine internal knowledge while preserving the published declaration contract and source-bound initialization plan. An open-bound witness shall remain open during a generic's closed-bound requirement check. A compiler shall base backend assumptions on established evidence, dominating validation, or explicit trust, and shall preserve required CPN26 terminal edges under its selected lowering. The [core transformation rules](#chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance) govern code motion, elimination, and folding.

### 10. Required semantic examples

```cpn
[[effects(none)]]
declare u32 identity(u32 n) noexcept;

[[requires(source.size() > 0)]]
[[effects(read(source))]]
declare u8 first(Span<const<u8>> source) noexcept;

[[effects(read(source), write(destination), trap(contract))]]
[[requires(destination.size() >= source.size())]]
declare void copy_into(Span<u8> destination, Span<const<u8>> source);
```

The first declaration shall require a valid nonempty span. Selecting checked entry validation shall add its ContractTrap boundary effect to the body's read(source) effect. Document mode shall retain the caller obligation. Copy_into shall additionally state its permitted overlap behavior under the region contract. Noexcept shall retain its language-exception meaning alongside the independent trap(contract) outlet.

```cpn
[[requires(divisor != 0), ensures(return_value >= 0)]]
[[effects(trap(numeric))]]
declare i32 bounded_quotient(i32 numerator, i32 divisor);
```

A bounded_quotient implementation choosing checked arithmetic shall include its possible NumericTrap in the stated effect bound. Establishing a nonzero divisor shall discharge the division-by-zero condition; the selected division operation shall separately require its signed-overflow policy and range conditions. Native ordinary arithmetic shall use its provider-declared effects under Section 3.2.

```cpn
[[effects(allocate(resource), write(destination))]]
declare Result<void, AllocError>
    initialize_buffer(ResourceRef resource, OwnedBuffer& destination);
```

Err shall be a normal result value. Initialize_buffer shall retain attempted-allocation and permitted-mutation effects. An implementation releasing old storage shall additionally admit deallocate(resource); old-element retirement shall contribute its actual throwing, terminal, or I/O effects under Chapter 25.

```cpn
[[ensures(return_value == input)]]
[[effects(none)]]
i32 identity_with_postcondition(i32 input) noexcept {
    return input;
}
```

The result shall be constructed once. Ensures shall read the still-live input parameter at the prepared-return boundary. A selected checked predicate shall contribute its possible ContractTrap to the contract-boundary descriptor.

The following completion distinctions are required:

| Boundary case | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| A return explicitly moves a parameter into its result. | Ensures sees the live parameter's current moved-from state and the constructed result, not a hidden copy of the entry value. |
| Body-local destruction fails before the prepared normal-return boundary. | The selected failure path governs the unpublished result before reaching ensures. |
| Ensures passes, then a parameter destructor propagates a permitted failure. | The caller receives no successful return; continuing cleanup retires the unpublished result without restoring consumed ownership. |
| Ensures evaluates to false under `check`. | ContractTrap occurs without parameter destruction or result rollback being added by the contract facility. |
| A Result-returning body constructs `Err`. | The ordinary normal-return path evaluates ensures for the Result value. |
| An async ensures check passes, then cancellation wins at successful-return commitment. | The uncommitted result is retired and Cancelled is published only after required cleanup; passing ensures did not publish Value. |
| A reference result designates a parameter-owned subobject that will die during exit. | The borrow/lifetime violation remains invalid even if the referent was readable during ensures. |

### 11. Conformance and boundary preservation

Each callable shared across a semantic boundary shall retain its canonical phase bounds, contract policy, parameter-position mapping, lifetime/ownership requirements, and ABI identity in its bound interface contract under Chapter 21. A consumer shall bind that contract, use a verified adapter, or apply the ordinary conservative opaque-import contract. Conformance shall preserve declared phase obligations independently of optional analysis depth and runtime validation selection.

---

<a id="chapter-25-effect-composition-boundaries"></a>

## CPN26 Effect Composition, Lifetime, and Foreign Boundaries Specification

### 1. Phase-aware effect composition

An expression's effects shall compose the operations it evaluates in source order, including argument/parameter admission, selected execution, result construction, and required cleanup. Chapter 24 owns effect categories and validation modes. The [abstract machine](#chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance) owns observations and permitted transformations. This chapter assigns the feature-specific phase boundaries.

A successful ordinary synchronous call shall follow this order:

| Stage | Operations attributed to the call |
| --- | --- |
| Callable selection | Evaluate the callable. |
| Parameter admission | For each parameter in order, evaluate its argument/default and initialize that parameter before the next argument. |
| Entry | Evaluate selected entry contracts, then enter the body. |
| Result preparation | Evaluate return expression and construct the unpublished result once. |
| Body retirement | Retire return-expression temporaries and remaining body locals. |
| Prepared normal return | Check ensures while parameters and admitted receiver designations remain live. |
| Final completion | Retire parameters and perform applicable exit-invariant checks. |
| Publication | Publish the completed result. |

Void returns omit a value construction; reference returns bind their admitted referent. Failure shall follow its selected outlet at the reached stage. A failure before ensures prevents that check; a later retirement failure still governs the unpublished result. Chapter 28 supplies the authorized cleanup and terminal behavior.

The caller's call-expression summary shall include its own argument expressions and parameter-admission work. The callee body bound governs its selected execution phase. Mandatory destination construction shall retain that attribution even when caller evaluation and parameter storage share a physical slot.

#### 1.1 Sequencing and effect algebra

A path's effect set shall be the union of its possible operations, including required cleanup. Branch summaries shall conservatively union reachable paths, while execution shall evaluate only selected branches. Composition shall retain source order and synchronization dependencies in addition to the set. Optional interprocedural inference shall follow Chapter 24's analysis mode; opaque calls shall use their bound summary.

A handled throw shall contribute the handler and other observed operations; escaping propagation shall contribute throw. Returning Err shall be ordinary result delivery. Required terminal actions shall remain represented on paths that end at that outlet. Reordering shall satisfy the core equivalence or expressly selected native-transformation contract.

#### 1.2 Destructors and generated operations

Generated/defaulted copy, move, destruction, Cleanup, and rollback shall compose the operations required by the selected member/base plan. A manual destructor shall include its reachable explicit and remainder obligations. A live moved-from object shall retain its eventual retirement effects.

Failure-boundary composition shall follow Chapter 28. A Release destruction boundary shall represent its terminal outlet when an exception escapes; a continuing aggregate boundary shall represent its permitted propagation/collection. An ordinary throwing call contributes throw; an actually selected local terminal boundary contributes its terminal effect. Explicit capture handles only propagation reaching its handler.

Storage reconstruction and responsibility changes shall contribute their actual generation, ownership, memory, and lifetime transitions. Whole shall retain Chapter 06's coordinator control effect.

### 2. Borrow regions, escape bounds, and ownership transitions

A borrow contract shall identify its lifetime source, admissible region, qualification, and validity interval. Ordinary raw pointers and aliases shall use the memory chapter's corresponding obligations. Parameter annotations describe the selected callable's permitted use.

| Annotation | Boundary guarantee |
| --- | --- |
| `[[noescape(p)]]` | Retention ends at the call, except the separately declared returned-borrow path. |
| `[[returns_borrowed_from(p)]]` | Returned access is bounded by the source lifetime and compatible qualification. |
| `[[consumes(p)]]` | Perform the selected ownership/responsibility transition under the API's success/failure contract. |
| `[[requires_initialized(slots...)]]` / `[[initializes(slots...)]]` | Apply Chapter 06's bound construction-state summary. |
| `[[lifecycle_effect(whole)]]` | Admit propagation of Chapter 06's Whole control effect. |

A returned borrow with several possible origins shall publish all of them; unresolved possible sources shall remain live until a permitted refinement selects the actual origin. Ordinary by-value source objects shall retain their selected moved-from and destruction contracts after a consuming operation.

#### 2.1 Additional retention contract

`[[retains(p, owner)]]` shall designate a named owning parameter or explicitly typed returned owner that may retain a borrow derived from p. Referent validity shall follow its own lifetime source; any mechanism prolonging that lifetime shall be explicitly part of the retention contract.

Independent retention beyond the call conflicts with noescape. The separately declared returns_borrowed_from path is admitted when it is the sole surviving designation. A retaining operation shall establish resource admission and last-use/quiescence obligations before publishing its retained handle. Failure shall follow the API's stated ownership guarantee. An opaque callback shall use its declared retention contract or an open conservative summary.

#### 2.2 Escape proof obligations

A returned, stored, captured, or task-transferred borrow shall cover every access admitted by its resulting interface. Evidence may be a static lifetime, a selected checked owner token, or an explicit external-lifetime obligation. Ordinary unknown obligations shall use Chapter 24's analysis classification and Chapter 08's ANOMALY policy. Required proof and definitely invalid lifetime rules retain their corresponding acceptance requirements.

Borrow copying, type substitution, const qualification, and handle movement shall preserve the original validity bound. A retained foreign callback shall keep its designated storage live until the provider acknowledges last use/quiescence. Explicit checked-view metadata shall follow that view's representation and resource contract.

#### 2.3 Transfers and failure atomicity

A consumes operation shall publish its success transition and failure responsibility. Its more specific storage, BigInt, collection, or Task/Thread guarantee governs which owner remains responsible on failure.

Ownership commitment and successful return publication are separate events. A committed in-place replacement shall retain its new owner through a later retirement failure. An unpublished returning/delivering value shall be retired on its permitted continuing failure path. Source consumption shall remain consumed, including Task delivery that subsequently retires its unpublished receiver. Attempted allocation and deallocation shall retain their selected resource effects, including a normal Err result.

### 3. Async admission, execution, and cancellation effects

An async callable shall publish separate admission and task-execution contracts. `effects` governs task execution, completion, and cleanup; `admission_effects` governs frame/support admission, capture transfer, additional parameter binding, and the cleanup these create. Each omitted bound is open. The admission attribute is admitted on async declarations.

```cpn
[[admission_effects(allocate(context))]]
[[effects(read(input), io, suspend, cancel_point)]]
declare async u32 fetch(std::task::Context context,
                        Span<const<u8>> input);
```

The input borrow shall remain valid for its execution-time uses. Resource attempts shall use the Context's selected domains. Capture transfer and additional parameter binding shall contribute their actual throw, terminal, and resource effects to admission.

The call expression shall follow Chapter 17: evaluate callable/Context, admit final frame storage, then transfer captures and evaluate/construct subsequent arguments and parameters. Explicit/default argument expressions remain caller-side effects, including a prvalue constructor using a frame parameter's final slot. A failed frame admission shall publish the prescribed failed Task before later argument evaluation. Start, join, await, and detach shall use their own later-call contracts.

Selected async requires checks shall execute after complete admission and before successful cold-call execution-initialization commitment and Created publication, under the admission caller's context. Selected ensures checks shall execute on prepared normal task return: construct the result, retire expression temporaries/body locals, check ensures while parameters/captures remain live, then retire those parameters/captures and perform final exit checks. Completion storage shall retain the ownership prescribed by the Task protocol.

A cancellation request shall take effect only at its admitted selection point. If cancellation wins the completion commitment, the unpublished result shall be retired before Cancelled publication. A selected language-failure or terminal outlet shall follow Chapter 28. The task body shall use its bound execution-context policy; explicit strict/status contexts retain their selected observations, while Native uses Chapter 04's native context contract.

#### 3.1 Cancellation checkpoint vs ordinary return

cancel_point shall admit cooperative cancellation at the lexical async checkpoint defined by Chapter 13. Acceptance shall select the required cleanup and Cancelled outcome. An ordinary helper may observe a token and return to that checkpoint. External retained-frame users shall acknowledge quiescence before frame release.

suspend, block, spawn, and cancel_point are separate effect permissions. A callable performing several of them shall admit each actual category. Progress and compensation guarantees shall come from the selected operation/provider contract.

#### 3.2 Thread and detached work effects

Thread creation or detached submission shall contribute spawn at admission. Joining, lock acquisition, and synchronized completion shall contribute synchronize and block where applicable. Close shall include admitted cleanup and completion-callback effects. Each callback shall execute under its declared entry context and failure boundary, including when invoked inline. Detached work shall retain its owned borrow and module-lifetime obligations.

### 4. Static initialization and consteval boundaries

A static initialization summary shall include initializer evaluation, construction, readiness dependencies, observable registration, and continuing failure cleanup. An initializer with external effects shall satisfy its cancellation/compensation contract or use the finish policy. Its readiness edge constrains execution order; the initializer's callable contract governs its other effects.

Constant-initialized nodes shall retain their logical dependency classification. Required constant evaluation shall use the admitted operations and resources of Chapter 10. An unevaluated branch contributes no execution effect; each selected compile-time path shall satisfy that evaluator. Generation shall validate emitted effect contracts at the declaration and completion stages in Chapter 23.

### 5. Foreign calls, callbacks, and native ABI

A foreign boundary shall satisfy its selected object-file, callable ABI, lifetime, failure, resource, and effect contracts. C/C++ consumers shall receive applicable requirements through the provider descriptor, compatible header, or explicit adapter. A foreign import with an unverified body shall use its declared external-contract obligation or the conservative open bound.

A stronger local checking adapter shall implement its own validation. A prohibited exception escape shall follow the selected foreign terminal boundary in Chapter 28; an explicit programmer handler may translate an admissible exception to a declared error value. A Result-to-C adapter shall apply its output-state and write-on-success contract. External side effects and allocator release authority shall retain their provider-defined ownership.

#### 5.1 Callback effects

Callback registration shall describe inline execution, concurrency/reentry, retention duration, execution agent, and relevant FP-context behavior. Registration and later callback execution shall have distinct phase contracts. Retained callbacks shall have a matching last-use/quiescence protocol and storage/code lifetime.

The selected callback adapter shall define context representation, calling convention, ownership, allocation, and failure boundary. A verified boundary or explicit wrapper shall supply any guaranteed termination behavior promised by a CPN26 noexcept callback interface.

### 6. Effect-aware generic and callable substitution

For candidate bound A and destination bound B, effect substitution shall require A to be a subset of B after normalizing parameter positions, receiver identity, and callable phase. It shall also satisfy borrow origins, retention, ownership, failure, value-contract variance, and ABI compatibility. Region names at equivalent parameter positions denote the same canonical binding; invocation-specific aliasing leaves that declared identity unchanged.

A compatible narrower bound may adapt to a wider bound. Strengthening an unverified bound shall require the corresponding proof or an adapter implementing that guarantee. A generic closed-bound requirement shall be established by its selected callable signature/witness under Chapter 27.

The optional std.effects module shall provide these compile-time queries:

| Query | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `effect_contract_of(FunctionInfo)` | Descriptor of the callable's public phase-specific bound, if available. |
| `subset(A, B)` | Compile-time Boolean under the standard normalization order. |
| `has(A, effect_kind)` | Whether A admits the requested category. |
| `is_open(A)` | Whether A is conservative/open rather than a closed upper bound. |
| `borrow_sources(FunctionInfo)` | Named/position-based returned-borrow sources and retention contracts. |
| `admission_effects_of(FunctionInfo)` | Bound for an admitted async callable's creation phase. |
| `execution_effects_of(FunctionInfo)` | Bound for the selected callable execution phase. |

Each query shall use accessible published contract data. Unavailable information shall produce its named capability/query error. Runtime descriptor materialization uses its separate selected operation.

#### 6.1 Type-constructor and associated effect substitution

A callable obtained through a constructor or associated projection shall satisfy the same phase and substitution rules. A public projected type retaining an input borrow shall expose that origin/retention contract in the generic signature. A type-equality proof supplies type identity; the corresponding operations shall establish their own value, lifetime, and ownership requirements.

### 7. Function pointer, closure, and virtual-boundary identity

A callable's semantic type shall retain the effect/lifetime contract defined by Chapters 10 and 24. The chosen native ABI or explicit context adapter shall define its machine representation. Closures shall retain their capture and invocation effects.

Virtual overrides shall preserve the base callable contract under Chapter 24's variance rules. Shared callable identities shall carry these requirements in their semantic boundary records under Chapter 21. A conflicting public contract shall require correction or an explicit compatible bridge before linkage. ABI layout and symbol effects shall follow the selected target profile.

### 8. Synchronization, I/O, and FP observability

Atomic and synchronization operations shall retain their selected memory-order and progress contracts under Chapter 13. The effect categories describe their permitted actions; operation descriptors supply lock-free, ownership, waiting, and cancellation details.

An I/O operation shall retain its published partial-success and resource effects. A prefix-producing write may return Err after committed output. Formatting that allocates shall admit its resource effect; serialization into an existing buffer shall describe its destination write and any additional effects.

Floating operations shall contribute fp_status/fp_control according to Chapter 24's vocabulary and Chapter 04's selected observability. Explicit Strict, Reproducible, report, try, and environment operations shall retain their specified status/control effects. Ordinary Native operations shall use the provider's native result, fault, subnormal, NaN, and relaxation contract without required local/sticky accounting. Later status inspection observes that declared provider state; it adds no retrospective strict requirement. Explicit strict boundary adapters shall isolate native clobber where their selected caller contract requires it.

### 9. Diagnostics and decision procedures

The checker shall use Chapter 24's single declared/proved/unknown classification and Chapter 08's diagnostic policy. Release local inference shall consume current-definition facts and bound summaries. Required callable/generic constraints shall use Chapter 27's standard decision procedure independently of optional inference depth.

#### 9.1 Transformation obligations

For each proposed transformation, the implementation shall preserve the observations selected by the affected contracts:

| Contract | Required preservation |
| --- | --- |
| Named checked/report/Result operation | Selected failure/value/status outlet and argument evaluation. |
| I/O and resource transition | Committed effects, owner changes, and specified failure guarantees. |
| Lifetime and borrow | Required cleanup, generation identity, and admitted access interval. |
| Async admission | Frame-failure boundary, argument evaluation, and task-phase separation. |
| Foreign callback | Its declared effects, retention, and entry boundary. |
| Explicit Strict/Reproducible arithmetic | The selected zero/NaN/status, rounding, and reduction contract. |
| Ordinary Native arithmetic | Its provider-permitted transformations and all independent source side effects, memory accesses, atomic events, and required fault behavior. |

### 10. Configuration, semantic records, and conformance

The bound callable contract shall retain phase bounds, normalized regions, ownership/borrow contracts, value-contract policy, function ABI, exception boundary, and effect vocabulary revision. Chapter 21 shall govern its semantic identity and optional external publication. The defining declaration shall bind semantic configuration; an importing diagnostic profile affects only the importer's permitted diagnostics.

A conforming effect implementation shall support its admitted syntax, normalization, redeclaration/override checking, open-bound behavior, phase composition, and selected diagnostics. Optional introspection or runtime checking shall follow the resolved capability set. Implementations shall preserve the selected core and feature contracts while choosing their internal analysis, state representation, and code generation.

<a id="chapter-26-advanced-generic-families"></a>

## CPN26 Higher-Order Generic Families and Associated Types Specification

### 1. Scope and invariant requirements

This chapter defines recursive type-constructor kinds, constructor expressions and partial application, associated entities, structural witnesses, and explicit public conformance declarations. The [ordinary generic rules](#chapter-10-types-functions-generics) own ordinary type identity and instantiation; [Chapter 27](#chapter-27-constraint-solver-inference) owns deduction, proof, candidate selection, and coherence checking.

A *type constructor* SHALL map an admitted finite argument sequence to an ordinary type. Its argument kinds may themselves describe type constructors, and its final parameter may accept a finite pack. A *conformance witness* shall identify a constraint application and the associated entities and operation contracts selected for its subject type. Both are compile-time entities. Their use shall preserve the selected ordinary type's numeric, lifecycle, ownership, and effect contracts. Runtime representation and explicit erased adapters follow [Chapter 21](#chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance).

### 2. Recursive kinds and constructor expressions

A kind SHALL be a finite structural tree. The admitted descriptors are `type`, `const Type`, and `typefn<kind-list>`. A constructor descriptor SHALL contain its argument-kind sequence and the ordinary-type result kind. A kind-list may be empty and may end in one repeated descriptor. A repeated descriptor SHALL accept a finite ordered sequence of arguments of that kind, including an empty sequence.

| Parameter or descriptor | Argument domain |
| --- | --- |
| `type T` | One canonical ordinary type. |
| `const Type N` | One admitted required constant of the declared type. |
| `typefn F<type>` | One constructor accepting one ordinary type. |
| `typefn H<typefn<type>, type>` | One constructor accepting a unary constructor and an ordinary type. |
| `typefn F<type...>` | One constructor with a final pack of ordinary types. |
| `typefn F<type, typefn<type>...>` | One constructor with a type argument followed by a pack of unary constructors. |
| `typefn... Fs<type>` | A generic parameter pack whose elements are unary constructors. |
| `typefn F<>` | One nullary constructor. Applying `F<>` yields its ordinary type. |

The checker SHALL recursively compare kinds by descriptor, canonical constant-parameter type, fixed-position order, and final-pack structure. Bound names SHALL be alpha-equivalent. The kind grammar SHALL admit every finite nesting depth for higher-order kinds. The configured normalization and arity resources SHALL bound checking work and report exhaustion under Chapter 27.

```cpn
generic<typefn F<type>, type T>
requires (ObjectType<F<T>> && CompleteType<F<T>>)
struct Cell {
    F<T> value;
};

generic<typefn F<type>, type T>
alias ApplyOne = F<T>;

generic<typefn H<typefn<type>, type>, typefn F<type>, type T>
alias ApplyHigher = H<F, T>;

generic<typefn F<type...>, type... Ts>
alias ApplyPack = F<Ts...>;
```

These constructs SHALL be compile-time mappings. Their applications SHALL retain the selected ordinary types' value, layout, lifetime, and effect contracts.

#### 2.1 Formation and full application

A constructor argument SHALL designate a generic record, union, fully defined alias family, a bound constructor parameter or projection, or a constructor expression defined below. Its declared signature SHALL match the required kind. Every fixed parameter SHALL count, including a defaulted position; a final pack SHALL remain a repeated descriptor. Constant-parameter types SHALL match canonically. A fixed signature and a variadic signature SHALL retain their respective shapes; an explicit constructor expression may map between them where the resulting applications are valid.

A constructor identity SHALL contain its canonical declaration or expression identity, kind, captured bindings, and meaning-affecting definition environment. Applying a generic alias-family constructor SHALL yield the mapped type's ordinary identity while preserving the alias-family identity when that constructor itself is an argument. A transparent constructor alias SHALL preserve its referenced constructor identity under Section 3.

A full application through a bound typefn SHALL supply its fixed positions and its final pack elements. The checker SHALL substitute them, select the owning family's published specialization, establish its requirements, and obtain the resulting ordinary type. A direct named-family application may additionally use that family's declared defaults. A required unavailable application SHALL fail type formation under Chapter 27's context rules.

A typefn generic parameter may have a constructor-expression default whose free names bind in its definition environment. An omitted argument SHALL use an admitted deduction or that default. A final constructor-parameter pack SHALL collect the remaining explicit constructor arguments in order. Each application of a member of that pack SHALL use its member kind.

#### 2.2 Explicit partial application

`partial_typefn<F, arguments...>` SHALL construct a residual constructor by binding a finite prefix of F's arguments. F SHALL first resolve to one constructor identity. Each supplied argument SHALL match the next fixed descriptor, or an element of its final repeated descriptor. The residual kind SHALL retain the remaining fixed descriptors and any final repeated descriptor.

```cpn
generic<type Left, type Right>
struct Pair {};

generic<type... Ts>
struct Tuple {};

generic<typefn F<type>, type T>
requires (ObjectType<F<T>> && CompleteType<F<T>>)
struct Holder {
    F<T> item;
};

alias IntPairHolder = Holder<partial_typefn<Pair, i32>, u8>;
```

Applying the residual constructor SHALL prepend its captured prefix and fully apply F. Binding all fixed positions of a fixed constructor SHALL produce a nullary constructor. A prefix entering a final pack SHALL retain an open residual pack and prepend the captured elements to each later application. Binding an empty prefix SHALL preserve F's constructor identity.

Residual identity SHALL use F's identity, the canonical bound prefix, and the residual kind. Repeated prefix application SHALL flatten to this canonical representation: prefix-binding a residual constructor SHALL append to its captured prefix. Family defaults SHALL remain explicit source choices; a residual constructor SHALL retain every unbound fixed position.

A bound ordinary constant SHALL preserve its actual value and declared type; a bound type or constructor SHALL preserve its canonical identity. Capturing an argument SHALL establish its kind and required constant validity. Requirements depending on later arguments SHALL be checked when the residual constructor is applied.

#### 2.3 Inline constructor mappings

`typefn<binder-list>(type-id)` SHALL form an inline constructor. Its binders SHALL use the generic type, constant, recursive typefn, and final-pack forms. The parentheses SHALL contain the resulting type expression. The mapping SHALL bind its other names, defaults used by named applications, and policies at its definition site.

```cpn
alias TextPairHolder = Holder<typefn<type U>(Pair<U, char>), i32>;

generic<typefn F<type>, typefn G<type>, type T>
alias ComposeAt = typefn<type U>(F<G<U>>)<T>;
```

Each application SHALL substitute the inline binders into the captured type expression and establish its ordinary type-formation requirements. The same constructor expression with the same captured arguments SHALL have one constructor identity. Separate expression declarations may retain different constructor identities while their applications yield equal ordinary types.

Formation of an inline mapping SHALL establish binder kinds, captured names, and the mapped expression's nondependent legality. Dependent type formation SHALL occur for each full application under its actual arguments and declared evidence. An inline mapping may bind arbitrary positions, reorder arguments, prepend or append pack elements, and compose constructors. A pack expansion SHALL preserve element order and require compatible lengths for packs expanded together. A final pack SHALL consume the remaining arguments of that mapping. The checker SHALL normalize constructor applications through the finite substitution and cycle rules in Chapter 27.

For `generic<type T, const usize N = 4> struct BufferFamily {};`, bare BufferFamily has kind `typefn<type, const usize>`. The expression `typefn<type T>(BufferFamily<T>)` SHALL expose a unary constructor whose body uses the captured default. The expression `typefn<type T>(BufferFamily<T, 4>)` SHALL expose its explicit-value counterpart. Both SHALL record their captured definition dependencies.

#### 2.4 Qualified names and dependent applications
