An applied parameter, inline expression, residual constructor, or associated projection SHALL have its established kind before argument binding. For `T::Something<U>`, accessible declarations or declared constraints SHALL establish Something's kind. An imported alias may preserve constructor kind. Definition-site lookup and the grammar's generic-delimiter rules SHALL classify the expression.

A required kind comparison SHALL inspect the finite kind structure. Application SHALL perform substitution at the bound constructor and retain the fixed family or witness catalogue. Higher-order constructor values SHALL be supplied explicitly, by an admitted direct deduction, or by a declared default; Chapter 27 defines the deduction boundary.

### 3. Type and constructor aliases

A nongeneric `alias Name = right-hand-side;` SHALL bind according to the right-hand side's established kind. An ordinary type SHALL create a transparent type alias. An unapplied family, bound typefn, constructor projection, partial expression, or inline mapping SHALL create a transparent constructor alias. Bare family names SHALL retain constructor kind; a full application, including an explicit empty argument list using family defaults, SHALL yield its resulting ordinary type.

```cpn
alias IntPair = partial_typefn<Pair, i32>;
alias ReversePair = typefn<type T>(Pair<T, i32>);
alias ConcretePair = IntPair<u8>;
```

The first two declarations SHALL preserve the identities of their constructor expressions. The third SHALL have the selected Pair application's ordinary type identity. The alias declaration SHALL retain its own declaration identity for visibility, publication, and reflection. Constructor matching and application SHALL follow the referenced constructor identity.

#### 3.1 Generic alias families

`generic<...> alias Name = type-id;` SHALL declare a compile-time alias family with an ordinary-type result. Its parameters and optional requires clause SHALL follow the ordinary generic declaration rules. Definition checking SHALL establish its bound names, kinds, and nondependent legality; each admitted full application SHALL form its dependent mapped type under its actual arguments and constraints.

The selected application shall have the resulting type's canonical identity, including its selected specialization. The alias family shall have a separate stable declaration identity for constructor arguments and witnesses. Thus `SameType<Alias<i32>, Underlying<i32>>` may hold while the two constructor declarations remain distinct.

An exported alias shall publish the type and constraint material needed to validate its permitted public applications. Its runtime layout and foreign compatibility shall be those of the selected underlying type. Recursive alias expansion shall satisfy the termination and cycle rules in Chapter 27.

### 4. Associated type and constant requirements

A constraint containing associated entities SHALL use its first formal parameter, an ordinary `type` parameter, as its single subject. Its remaining type, constant, and constructor parameters SHALL be additional witness arguments. A pure structural constraint may use any admitted parameter sequence. A constraint may declare associated entities:

```cpn
constraint Sequence<type S> {
    associated type Item;
    associated const usize StaticExtent;
    expression (const<S>& source) {
        source.size() -> usize;
    }
};
```

`associated type Item;` SHALL require one ordinary type binding. `associated const usize StaticExtent;` SHALL require one admitted constant of that type. An associated declaration may provide a default binding with `=`, evaluated under that constraint's captured environment after substitution. The complete constraint application SHALL own the associations; its subject SHALL retain its ordinary members and representation.

`Sequence<S>::Item` and `Sequence<S>::StaticExtent` SHALL project the selected association. A concrete projection SHALL resolve one witness under Section 5; a symbolic projection SHALL use its declared constraint bound. A projected constant may participate in required constant evaluation. The full constraint argument tuple, including every additional parameter, SHALL enter the witness key.

Inside the declaring constraint, an unqualified associated identifier shall denote that constraint's associated declaration. Another generic definition shall establish the relevant bound:

```cpn
generic<type S>
requires (Sequence<S>)
alias SequenceItem = Sequence<S>::Item;
```

The alias yields the projected ordinary type. An operation such as `source.first()` shall separately have a supporting structural expression requirement or ordinary declaration. Additional associated-type relationships shall use explicit requirements, for example `requires (SameType<Sequence<S>::Item, i32>);`. Access to a private binding shall require its ordinary published authority.

#### 4.1 Associated type constructors

`associated typefn Name<kind-list>;` shall require a constructor binding with the kinds in Section 2:

```cpn
constraint Rebindable<type T> {
    associated typefn Rebind<type>;
};
```

For a selected conformance to `Rebindable<Box<i32>>`, `Rebindable<Box<i32>>::Rebind<u8>` shall apply its bound constructor and yield an ordinary type. The bare projection `Rebindable<Box<i32>>::Rebind` shall retain typefn kind and may supply a matching constructor parameter. Its applications shall satisfy the selected family constraints, completeness, constant-evaluation, and public-reachability requirements.

### 5. Structural and explicit witnesses

The checker SHALL obtain a concrete witness from the subject owner's bound public catalogue and the structural fallback defined here. Explicit `satisfy` declarations SHALL provide customized association tables or certify a chosen contract:

```cpn
struct SampleBuffer {
    usize size() const { return 4; }
};

satisfy Sequence<SampleBuffer> {
    type Item = i32;
    const usize StaticExtent = 4;
};
```

For one candidate, the checker SHALL form an association table of bound recipes using this precedence for each required entity:

1. The candidate's explicit binding, when present.
2. The associated declaration's default, when present.
3. The subject's uniquely resolved, accessible nested entity of the same name and required kind.

A nested alias or type SHALL supply an ordinary type association. A required constant SHALL supply its declared canonical constant type and value. A nested generic family, constructor alias, or associated constructor expression SHALL supply a matching typefn association. The checker SHALL evaluate the candidate condition and its selected requirements using the recipes needed by that evaluation. A condition that evaluates False SHALL end that candidate's applicability check. An applicable candidate SHALL complete every required binding and establish all structural and Boolean requirements before witness commitment.

The structural fallback SHALL use the same procedure with an empty explicit table. Thus an ordinary type exposing the required operations and nested entities may satisfy the constraint directly. Declared defaults may map differently named members or derive associations under the constraint's captured contract.

```cpn
struct NativeSequence {
    alias Item = i32;
    static constexpr usize StaticExtent(4);
    usize size() const { return 4; }
};

alias NativeItem = Sequence<NativeSequence>::Item;
```

The example SHALL obtain its associations structurally. The size expression SHALL separately satisfy the declared result and receiver contract. A constraint containing structural requirements alone SHALL use the same requirement checking with an empty association table.

#### 5.1 Conformance priority and selection

Each explicit `satisfy` declaration SHALL have one fixed conformance priority. The registered leading attribute `[[conformance_priority(N)]]` SHALL set that priority to its nondependent required integer constant N in the inclusive range 0 through 4294967295. An omitted attribute SHALL supply priority 0. The attribute SHALL apply to an authored `satisfy` declaration, and its value SHALL bind at declaration checking. Duplicate priority attributes, a dependent value, or a value outside the admitted range SHALL produce a declaration error. This compile-time metadata value SHALL have the same ordering on every target.

A bare integer literal SHALL supply its exact literal value to priority admission. A named constant or compound expression SHALL first complete ordinary required integer constant evaluation under its captured definition policy. Admission SHALL compare that mathematical result with the priority interval. The admitted priority SHALL be compiler metadata independently of target integer storage or runtime object materialization.

Priority comparison SHALL apply to the entries considered for one concrete witness request in its bound owner catalogue. Entries in unrelated catalogues may reuse the same integer. Equal priorities among entries whose concrete heads or conditions are mutually exclusive SHALL use the ordinary applicability rules.

Chapter 27 SHALL select each concrete witness by visiting head-matching entries in descending priority tiers. One established entry in the first successful tier SHALL supply the witness. Several established entries in that tier SHALL produce ambiguity. A tier whose entries all produce False SHALL pass selection to the next tier. Exhausting the tiers SHALL request structural fallback. Conformance ranking SHALL use the declared integer priorities; the separately defined function-overload and type-specialization rules SHALL govern those other selections.

Malformed, cyclic, unestablished required-proof, and exhausted-resource outcomes in a visited tier SHALL retain Chapter 27's distinct consequences. Publication SHALL establish every entry's nondependent legality. Dependent requirements in lower tiers SHALL remain demand-driven after an earlier tier supplies the witness.

An explicit association table may omit entities supplied by defaults or nested matches. Every completed table SHALL have one well-kinded, accessible, finite binding for each required entity. Checking the constraint's own associated projections within a candidate SHALL use that provisional table. A dependency that recursively requests selection of the same unresolved witness key SHALL follow Section 8's cycle rule.

##### 5.1.1 Design rationale and catalogue coordination (informative)

Fixed integer priorities give the conformance selector an explicit ordering key. Grouping and comparing these keys determines the order in which the checker visits tiers; head matching, concrete requirement checking, and witness validation remain necessary. The design favors a small, directly implementable selection procedure.

An integer records an absolute rank. Authors express an intended relationship such as one entry taking precedence over another by choosing the corresponding ranks. This places coordination work on the owner of a catalogue assembled by multiple authors. Independently chosen ranks can create an unintended precedence or an equal-priority ambiguity when entries overlap. Continued insertion of intermediate or higher-precedence entries can consume gaps and encourage increasingly large ranks. The finite priority range makes this an explicit library-maintenance constraint.

A catalogue maintainer can centralize named priority constants, document the purpose of each tier, and review newly overlapping entries against that policy. Reserving gaps or allocating ranges to contributors can reduce routine coordination, while later additions still require agreement on precedence. Equal ranks are useful for alternatives with concretely exclusive conditions. The owner can reuse the same numerical conventions in unrelated catalogues, whose selections remain independent.

Priority assignments form part of the published catalogue contract. Changing them can change witness selection; even an order-preserving renumbering changes the identity material specified by Chapter 27. A catalogue revision therefore needs the same dependency and compatibility review as other changes to its conformance contract. These coordination costs are a deliberate tradeoff of explicit scalar ordering, and the language's simple selection procedure leaves them with catalogue authors.

#### 5.2 Ownership and catalogue binding

The subject's canonical nominal type or family owner SHALL control its public conformance catalogue. That owner may publish a conformance to a foreign constraint. A constraint owner may publish conformances for its own types and for primitive or built-in families assigned to its registered standard-capability domain. An owning scope needing a different custom public conformance for another owner's type SHALL expose its own nominal adapter; structural satisfaction remains available from accessible declared members.

A family conformance for `Box<T>` SHALL belong to Box's canonical catalogue. `export satisfy`, or an equivalent export block, SHALL publish it. Publication SHALL validate declaration identity, ownership, signature, priority, and nondependent requirements and record the complete candidate set. Overlapping patterns SHALL be admitted; each required concrete use SHALL perform Section 5.1's selection. Ordinary duplicate-definition rules SHALL govern duplicate canonical declaration identities.

A private conformance SHALL concern a private nominal subject in its owning compilation scope and preserve its declared visibility. Exported uses SHALL publish the witness contract they require or expose an explicit public opaque adapter.

For a known subject, a generic definition SHALL capture the required catalogue identity and revision. For a symbolic subject, its declared constraint bound SHALL capture the subject-owner catalogue-selection recipe. Substitution SHALL obtain that catalogue from the actual canonical type argument's published owner contract and freeze its exact identity in the instance. Structural member lookup SHALL use that same subject contract. A later unrelated import SHALL retain these inputs; a catalogue revision becomes a new bound input at the appropriate recompilation boundary. Existing bound projections and emitted instances SHALL retain their selected witnesses.

#### 5.3 Conditional conformance and constructor binding

```cpn
generic<type T>
requires (CompleteType<T>)
satisfy Rebindable<Box<T>> {
    typefn Rebind<type U> = Box<U>;
};
```

The subject owner SHALL publish this conditional entry. Its local constructor binder SHALL follow Section 2's recursive kind and pack rules and map U to `Box<U>`. A conditionally applicable entry SHALL use its declared requirements during selection; the selected constructor's applications SHALL establish their resulting type requirements.

A specialized entry may provide a different association for a concrete subject or a narrower admitted pattern. Its author SHALL select a higher priority when that entry is intended to take precedence over another applicable entry. The selected entry SHALL establish the complete associated and callable contract it advertises.

```cpn
constraint ElementSource<type S> {
    associated type Item;
};

generic<type T>
struct Pocket {
    alias Item = T;
};

generic<type T>
satisfy ElementSource<Pocket<T>> {
    type Item = T;
};

[[conformance_priority(1)]]
satisfy ElementSource<Pocket<i32>> {
    type Item = u32;
};
```

`ElementSource<Pocket<i32>>::Item` SHALL be u32 through the priority-1 entry. Another `Pocket<T>` SHALL use the priority-0 entry when its requirements hold. Giving both matching entries priority 0 SHALL produce ambiguity for the i32 application. Their textual order SHALL preserve these results.

#### 5.4 Structural fallback provenance

Chapter 27 SHALL diagnose a successful structural fallback reached after all head-matching explicit entries produce False. Diagnostic `GEN001` SHALL use Chapter 08's default ANOMALY classification and diagnostic configuration. A purely structural use whose bound catalogue has no head-matching explicit entry SHALL use its ordinary structural result.

For example, consider a separate owner catalogue containing the following sole explicit entry for the preceding `ElementSource` and `Pocket` declarations:

```cpn
generic<type T>
requires (SameType<T, u8>)
satisfy ElementSource<Pocket<T>> {
    type Item = u8;
};

alias SelectedItem = ElementSource<Pocket<i32>>::Item;
```

The head SHALL match `Pocket<i32>`, its condition SHALL evaluate False, and structural fallback SHALL obtain i32 from the nested Item alias. The successful SelectedItem binding SHALL produce `GEN001` with that provenance. Its diagnostic SHALL distinguish an inapplicable explicit entry from the structural witness actually selected.

### 6. Dependent projection and use-site obligations

A generic requiring `Sequence<S>` shall use its Item as a symbolic ordinary type while checking the definition. Instantiation shall substitute the selected witness binding under the captured environment.

| Source notation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `S::Item` | Ordinary accessible nested type of S. |
| `Sequence<S>::Item` | Associated type from the selected Sequence conformance. |
| `Sequence<S>::StaticExtent` | Constant from that conformance. |
| `Rebindable<S>::Rebind` | Associated constructor of typefn kind. |
| `Rebindable<S>::Rebind<U>` | Ordinary type produced by that constructor. |

An explicit `SameType<S::Item, Sequence<S>::Item>` requirement may relate the first two forms. When multiple constraints declare the same associated name, an external use shall qualify the projection with its constraint application. The chosen witness shall supply that projection.

A proved associated-type equality shall permit type substitution under Chapter 27. Each resulting value operation shall independently satisfy its value category, object state, lifetime, and effect requirements.

### 7. Structural witnesses and callable contracts

An expression requirement shall match the exact result type and value category specified by Chapter 10. A callable witness shall record the selected declaration or intrinsic, generic arguments, receiver qualifiers, signature, effect bounds, nonthrowing guarantee, and returned-borrow provenance.

The checker shall establish the required callable relationship under [Chapter 25](#chapter-25-effect-composition-boundaries). A closed effect bound requires corresponding evidence; merely naming an open callable in a satisfy table leaves that obligation unestablished. Ownership, destruction responsibility, and foreign-call guarantees shall come from the operation's actual contract or an explicit conforming adapter.

A symbolic associated result shall remain part of the required signature until concrete witness selection substitutes its binding. The generic body shall use the operations supplied by its declared requirements and ordinary language rules.

### 8. Associated-type recursion and well-foundedness

Associated bindings may depend on completed immutable constants and constructor applications. The evaluator shall resolve those dependencies using Chapter 27's cycle and termination rules. A self-projection such as `type Item = Sequence<S>::Item;` requires an independent completed nominal boundary to terminate resolution.

Recursive nominal families may use legal pointer and reference members. Every required value layout shall remain finite and complete under Chapter 10. Constraint, alias, reflection, and generation dependencies shall use their shared staged graph; required completion shall establish a complete witness within the configured resource limit.

### 9. Borrowing, ownership, and lifetime interaction

A projected type shall retain its concrete storage and borrowing obligations. A returned `Sequence<S>::Item&` shall identify its source region under Chapter 25. A generic returning a borrowing wrapper shall publish that source relationship even when its element type varies by witness.

The selected concrete type's copy, move, destructor, numerical, and allocator contracts shall govern those operations. Sharing a constructor family establishes the mapping relationship; each application's operation contracts remain independently checked.

### 10. Publication, ABI, and optimization

A public interface SHALL publish its recursive constructor kinds, pack shapes, constructor-expression mappings and captured arguments, constraints, catalogue bindings, and each explicit entry's conformance priority. A known subject SHALL carry its bound catalogue; a symbolic subject SHALL carry Chapter 27's subject-owner resolution recipe. A completed instance SHALL record its frozen concrete catalogue and selected witness identities. Consumers shall bind the published recipe or completed contract under its definition environment. Changing an associated binding or selected priority contract that changes a public type, ABI, or effects requires a compatible versioned bridge or an incompatible-interface diagnostic.

Publication here SHALL expose the semantic contract to its admitted consumers. The selected compilation and contract-export capabilities SHALL govern its internal transport or standardized external representation under Chapters 11, 21, and 29.

The instance identity in Chapter 10 SHALL additionally include canonical constructor expressions and captured bindings, pack lengths and ordered elements, selected conformance witnesses, and associated bindings relevant to the emitted instance. A structural witness SHALL identify the constraint application, subject, bound catalogue, and canonical default/member/operation declarations used to establish it. Code sharing shall preserve the observations defined by Chapter 21. An explicit erased adapter shall publish its runtime representation, ownership, lifetime, and call contract separately.

A selected `F<T>` shall meet the particular foreign ABI profile before use at a compatible boundary. Native object emission and explicit C/C++ adapters follow [Chapter 09](#chapter-09-native-interoperability).

### 11. Capability control and diagnostics

[Chapter 08](#chapter-08-runtime-configuration) owns the capability domains and defaults. `generic.higher_kinds` controls typefn parameters, recursive constructor kinds, constructor packs, and constructor expressions. `generic.associated_entities` controls associated entities, structural associated witnesses, and explicit conformance. Their use SHALL require the corresponding explicit capability selection. Ordinary type and constant parameters, their packs, generic functions, and structural constraints SHALL retain their Core meaning independently.

A use shall have its required capabilities at parsing, checking, import, and instantiation. Required compilation-resource failures shall use Chapter 27's distinct resource outcome.

| Case | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| A constructor accepts another constructor | Recursively match its finite kind and establish the full application. |
| A fixed kind receives a family with a defaulted second position | Compare the full fixed signature; an explicit mapping may bind the default and expose unary kind. |
| A variadic constructor receives an empty final pack | Apply it with that empty ordered sequence. |
| A constructor-parameter pack receives several constructors | Bind each kind and preserve source order. |
| A prefix binds every fixed constructor parameter | Produce a nullary residual constructor. |
| A prefix enters a final pack | Preserve a residual repeated descriptor and prepend the captured elements. |
| A structural subject supplies all associations and operations | Establish the fallback witness when the explicit candidate set is empty. |
| Two explicit conformances overlap at different priorities | Visit the higher tier first and select its unique established entry, or continue after all its entries produce False. |
| The first successful priority tier has several established entries | Report ambiguity at that use. |
| An earlier successful tier leaves lower dependent requirements unvisited | Preserve the selected witness and the lower entries' declaration checks. |
| Every head-matching explicit entry is False and structural fallback succeeds | Select the structural witness and produce GEN001 under the diagnostic policy. |
| No explicit head matches and structural fallback succeeds | Select the structural witness through ordinary structural checking. |
| Associated bindings form an unresolved cycle | Report the cycle under required type formation. |
| A declared compilation budget is exhausted | Report Resource exhausted separately from False. |
| A caller adds an import | Existing generic definitions retain their bound catalogues and selections. |
| A required constructor capability is unavailable | Report the capability requirement at its use. |

### 12. Conformance requirements

An enabled implementation shall accept well-formed declarations within its published capabilities and resource limits, establish recursive kinds and associated bindings, validate catalogue authority, select coherent witnesses at required uses, and preserve the selected numeric, lifecycle, ABI, and effect contracts. The checker shall report required-proof and resource outcomes using Chapter 27 and the diagnostic policy in Chapter 08.

---

<a id="chapter-27-constraint-solver-inference"></a>

## CPN26 Constraint Solving, Type Inference, and Coherence Specification

### 1. Scope and required determinism

This chapter owns generic deduction, requirement checking, constrained candidate selection, type-specialization selection, and witness-coherence checking. [Chapter 10](#chapter-10-types-functions-generics) owns ordinary type and declaration identity, lookup, and conversion ranks. [Chapter 26](#chapter-26-advanced-generic-families) owns constructor kinds and associated declarations.

For a fixed source, published interface set, target, and effective configuration, the checker shall produce the same successful bindings and candidate selection independently of optimization, worker scheduling, physical source path, process address, and import order. It shall use the standardized proof procedure and report required compilation-resource limits separately.

Required type and generic proofs remain part of language validity under every analysis preset. The local or interprocedural modes in [Chapter 24](#chapter-24-contracts-effects) govern optional analysis of ordinary programmer obligations. The solver shall classify its required proof outcomes by Section 3.

### 2. Constraint proposition model

A constraint shall combine the following admitted propositions:

| Proposition | Required evidence or evaluation |
| --- | --- |
| A constant Boolean expression | Required evaluation under its captured environment. |
| A named constraint application | Expansion of its declared requirements at canonical arguments. |
| A structural type or expression requirement | The specified type or operation contract. |
| A core type predicate, including SameType | The predicate's defined language relation. |
| An associated projection or witness requirement | A declared symbolic bound or a selected concrete conformance. |
| Negation, conjunction, or disjunction | Standard Boolean composition of admitted propositions. |
| An effect, ownership, category, or nonthrowing requirement | The corresponding bound callable contract. |

A canonical atom shall include its predicate kind, declaration or intrinsic identity, canonical type/value/constructor arguments, and meaning-affecting definition policy. Renaming a bound parameter shall preserve its position and atom identity. Same-spelled predicates owned by different declarations shall retain distinct identities.

Normalization shall substitute the named constraint's parameters and expand its requirements under its immutable definition environment. It shall preserve structural-operation and associated-projection identities, and evaluate only the branches selected by the required constant-evaluation rules.

#### 2.1 Boolean normalization and subsumption

Subsumption shall use propositional implication over equal canonical atoms after named-constraint expansion. Boolean constants, negations, and duplicate conjuncts or disjuncts shall follow ordinary propositional identities.

For symbolic ordering, `N > 0` and `N >= 1` are distinct atoms. For concrete applicability, each predicate shall evaluate at the selected N under its captured numerical policy. An ordering proof that requires an additional mathematical equivalence remains unestablished by the standard procedure.

If neither constraint propositionally implies the other, the checker shall leave their relative constraint rank tied. Section 5 shall resolve the resulting candidate set using the other standard ranks or report ambiguity.

#### 2.2 Type equalities and projections

Proved type identities shall form an equality relation within their evidence scope. The checker may substitute equal types through pointers, references, fixed arrays, and well-formed constructor applications. The resulting value operations shall still satisfy their ordinary conversion and object requirements.

A proposition involving `Sequence<T>::Item` shall first have a declared Sequence bound or a selected witness. Equality of two resulting ordinary types shall preserve the distinct declaration identities of the constructors that produced them.

Successful equality closure shall be finite. Infinite alias expansion, an infinite required value layout, or an invalid witness cycle shall fail under the corresponding type-formation rule.

### 3. Applicability and proof outcomes

The checker shall perform a concrete generic use in this semantic order:

1. Bind nondependent names and catalogue identities at the definition site.
2. Bind explicit arguments and perform the deductions admitted by Section 4.
3. Establish recursive parameter kinds, fixed and final-pack shapes, visibility, capabilities, and constant domains under Chapter 26.
4. Select required owning-family specializations and unique conformance witnesses.
5. Substitute canonical arguments and associated bindings into requirements.
6. Evaluate required constant predicates under the captured target and numerical policy.
7. Establish structural signatures, receiver categories, effects, borrow origins, and required operations from the available evidence.
8. Check the selected body under its immutable definition contract.

Each checking operation shall yield one of these outcomes:

| Outcome | Meaning and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Established | The proposition or operation has the required evidence; checking may use it. |
| False | A well-formed concrete predicate is false, or a declared structural operation is absent or incompatible; that candidate is inapplicable. |
| Unestablished | The declared symbolic domain supplies insufficient evidence; the dependent operation remains unavailable, and a use requiring that proof fails. |
| Malformed | Grammar, nondependent binding, required declaration legality, or catalogue coherence is invalid; compilation reports the error. |
| Resource exhausted | A required evaluation or solver step exceeds its configured resource limit; compilation reports a distinct resource error. |

Only the False outcome removes an otherwise well-formed candidate through requirement applicability. Once a body is selected, its invalid operation is a body error. Required constraints and explicit proof requests shall use this table even when ordinary optional analysis would report an unknown programmer obligation as ANOMALY.

#### 3.1 Short-circuiting and errors

Required Boolean evaluation shall visit the branches selected by ordinary short-circuit rules. Both branches shall retain their parsing, nondependent binding, and declaration-legality obligations. The explicit `if constexpr` rule in Chapter 10 supplies the corresponding dependent-operation branch facts.

A required evaluation reaching Numeric Trap, another terminal failure, or an inadmissible operation shall fail evaluation. A returned Result error remains an ordinary value. Its explicit success or error predicate may yield a Boolean requirement; Result itself requires that explicit interpretation.

### 4. Generic argument deduction

Deduction shall match formal type structure against the actual typed argument's canonical type and value category:

| Formal form | Deduction rule |
| --- | --- |
| By-value T | Deduce the adjusted source value type using Chapter 10's top-level qualification rule. |
| `T&`, `const<T>&`, or `T&&` | Apply the stated reference and category requirement. |
| `forward T` | Deduce U& for an lvalue U and qualified U for an expiring expression; explicit forwarding restores the source category. |
| `T[N]` | Deduce the complete element type and exact constant extent. |
| A repeated parameter | Require one identical canonical deduction at all occurrences. |
| A final type or constant pack | Deduce its ordered elements under the declared kind; include its length in instance identity. |
| `typefn F<...>` | Use an explicit constructor expression, direct canonical-argument deduction below, or its declared default; establish the recursive kind. |
| A final typefn parameter pack | Bind its explicit or directly deduced ordered constructor arguments under the element kind; include its length and identities in instance identity. |
| A parameter appearing only in an associated projection, computed expression, or result context | Require an independent admitted deduction or an explicit argument. |

When a formal and actual ordinary type share one known nominal generic family, the checker SHALL compare the canonical generic arguments stored in that family instance. A formal constructor parameter in one such argument position SHALL deduce the actual stored constructor identity and its kind. For example, matching `Holder<F,T>` against the canonical instance `Holder<Vec,i32>` SHALL deduce F as Vec and T as i32 when Holder's published parameter kinds identify those positions. A final constructor pack in such a known position SHALL deduce the stored ordered sequence. Repeated deductions SHALL agree canonically.

A composed constructor expression in a formal argument position SHALL be compared after its parameters are independently bound. A parameter appearing solely through a constructor's ordinary result SHALL require an independent binding. These rules use preserved family arguments as evidence; actual record layout or result-type similarity supplies its ordinary type identity alone.

The checker SHALL use these structural matches and the constructor expressions explicitly supplied by source. A constructor appearing solely through the ordinary type produced by its application SHALL obtain its argument independently or from a declared default. An explicit argument SHALL fix that parameter, then participate in ordinary constraint and call-conversion checking at every occurrence. Inline and partial constructors SHALL normalize by applying their captured mappings, while constructor identity SHALL follow Chapter 26.

#### 4.1 Contextual typing and literals

A concrete parameter type may provide an untyped numeric expression's context under the numeric rules. Deduction of an otherwise unconstrained value type from an untyped expression shall first use the resolved default literal type. An already typed value shall retain its type for deduction.

`auto name(expression);` shall use Chapter 10's value-type deduction. The established result may be an associated type; its object construction and lifetime remain ordinary operations on that selected type.

An exported generic return type shall be expressible using its declared constraints and reachable public interface material. An implementation-private type or proof requires publication of the necessary contract or an explicit public opaque interface.

### 5. Overload candidate selection

The checker shall select a call before evaluating its runtime arguments:

1. Form the reachable declaration set using Chapter 10's lexical and definition-site lookup.
2. Check callable kind, receiver category, required arity, pack binding, generic kinds, and explicit arguments.
3. Deduce permitted arguments and evaluate each candidate's declared requirements.
4. Remove False candidates and report malformed or resource outcomes using Section 3. A deleted or inaccessible declaration shall remain in the set until selected-declaration validation.
5. Compare Chapter 10's conversion ranks argument by argument. One candidate has a better conversion sequence exactly when every argument is at least as good and at least one is better.
6. For indistinguishable conversion ranks, prefer an applicable strictly more specialized generic pattern or a strictly stronger normalized constraint. Otherwise prefer a nongeneric declaration over an otherwise identical unconstrained generic declaration.
7. Select the unique best declaration, or report ambiguity. Validate its access, deletion status, effects, ownership, lifetime, nonthrowing guarantee, ABI, and body.

A declared target function-pointer contract may select an overload address under Chapter 10. Ordinary call ranking shall use the arguments and declared receiver requirements; its result type alone supplies no additional preference. Qualified names and explicit generic arguments may restrict the candidate set.

Two equally ranked applicable predicates remain tied unless the standard subsumption procedure orders them. Declaration position, body size, and estimated runtime cost leave that tie unchanged.

#### 5.1 Constraint subsumption examples

```cpn
constraint Readable<type T> {
    expression (const<T>& value) {
        value.read() -> i32;
    }
};

constraint ReadableAndSized<type T> {
    requires (Readable<T>);
    expression (const<T>& value) {
        value.size() -> usize;
    }
};
```

For identical parameters and conversion ranks, ReadableAndSized is stronger because its normalized requirements entail Readable's identical requirements. A selected type shall still supply the required operations.

Overloads constrained by symbolic `N > 0` and `N >= 1` remain tied by constraint rank. At a concrete positive N, both may be applicable; another standard rank or an explicit source selection must distinguish them.

### 6. Type-specialization and conformance selection

An owning type family SHALL select among its published specializations by structural pattern specificity followed by standard constraint subsumption. Selection SHALL yield one unique best applicable entry. The primary definition SHALL serve as the fallback when its own requirements hold and the catalogue contains no better applicable entry. An ambiguous set or invalid selected body SHALL fail that use.

For type specialization and the pattern rank in Section 5, structural specificity SHALL compare head patterns using finite structural matching. Pattern A is strictly more specific than B when B's parameter pattern matches A's symbolic head and the converse match fails. Concrete nominal constructors, fixed arguments, enabled constructor kinds, and ordered pack shapes SHALL participate in that comparison. An identity or expression that this matcher leaves unestablished SHALL leave that relative pattern rank tied. Constraint ordering SHALL use Section 2.1's normalized symbolic requirements. Explicit conformance selection SHALL instead use the fixed priority algorithm below.

#### 6.1 Conformance selection by priority

A public conformance catalogue SHALL admit overlapping head patterns. Every entry SHALL carry Chapter 26's conformance priority, with 0 as the default. For one required concrete constraint application, selection SHALL proceed as follows:

1. Obtain the complete bound owner catalogue and group its entries by equal priority. Visit the groups in descending numeric order. One group SHALL constitute one priority tier.
2. In the visited tier, match the complete subject and additional arguments against each entry's head using Section 4's direct argument deduction. A definite structural mismatch SHALL exclude that entry. A matching head SHALL bind its parameters and provisional association recipes. An unresolved required head match SHALL retain Section 3's proof or resource outcome. A tier with zero matching heads SHALL advance to the next tier.
3. For each head-matching entry in the visited tier, evaluate its declared condition under the short-circuit rules. A condition that produces False SHALL complete that entry as False. For an established condition, complete the required associations and establish the constraint's full requirements, evaluating each association recipe when that checking needs it.
4. Establish the complete result of the visited tier. False SHALL remove that entry from that tier's established set. A required-proof failure, malformed dependent use, dependency cycle, or resource exhaustion SHALL produce its distinct error for the required witness. Several established entries SHALL produce ambiguity. Exactly one established entry SHALL become the selected witness. A tier whose head-matching entries all produce False SHALL advance to the next tier.
5. After the tiers are exhausted, establish the structural fallback with an empty explicit association table. Its established, False, or required-error result SHALL become the result of that witness request. A required projection or operation whose constraint is False SHALL fail its corresponding requirement.
6. Commit an established witness's identity, associated bindings, callable evidence, bound catalogue, and selection provenance together.

The first successful tier SHALL complete conformance selection. Lower tiers' concrete head matches, dependent conditions, and association recipes SHALL remain unvisited for that request; their nondependent legality SHALL already have been checked when their declarations entered the catalogue. A selected witness's later invalid use SHALL produce that use's required error under its committed contract.

Conformance priority SHALL be the complete ordering key among matched entries. Head matching SHALL determine argument bindings and eligibility. Conditions SHALL determine applicability. These steps SHALL keep conformance ranking independent of pairwise pattern comparison or predicate implication. Equal priorities SHALL retain their tie until concrete applicability yields one established entry or an ambiguity error. Declaration order, import traversal, and optional optimizer discoveries SHALL preserve the result.

Catalogue publication SHALL validate declaration identity, ownership, enabled kinds, fixed priority, and nondependent legality. Changing a priority SHALL change the catalogue's semantic contract. Selected type specializations and selected structural or explicit witnesses SHALL enter instance identity independently.

#### 6.2 Structural fallback provenance

A successful structural witness SHALL produce diagnostic `GEN001` when its selection visited at least one head-matching explicit entry and every such entry produced False. The diagnostic SHALL identify the requiring use, canonical constraint application, bound owner catalogue, head-matching declarations, the established False reason for each entry, and the selected structural bindings or operations. Chapter 08 SHALL determine its default ANOMALY severity and configured presentation, suppression, or promotion.

An owner catalogue's unrelated head patterns SHALL contribute their definite mismatch outcome alone. A structural witness formed with zero head-matching entries SHALL use ordinary structural checking. Selecting a lower-priority explicit entry SHALL preserve its explicit provenance. A structural fallback that itself produces False SHALL retain that False outcome. A visited ambiguity, required-proof failure, malformed use, dependency cycle, or exhausted resource SHALL retain its required error. These outcomes distinguish successful alternative structural selection from explicit selection, absence of conformance, and failed checking.

An implementation may coalesce GEN001 occurrences for one canonical witness key within a compilation request. The reported diagnostic SHALL retain at least one requiring-use location and identify coalesced uses. A successful witness cache entry SHALL retain its selection provenance, including the False explicit entries. Reusing the entry SHALL apply the current request's diagnostic configuration, so caching and checking order preserve the required diagnostic outcome.

#### 6.3 Witness coherence and semantic publication

An owning compilation scope SHALL retain canonical identifiers and semantic contracts for the catalogues needed by its constraints. A generic definition SHALL bind known catalogue identities together with its constraint contracts. A symbolic subject bound SHALL bind the subject-owner selection recipe; at instantiation, the actual canonical type argument's owner contract SHALL supply the exact catalogue and structural member contract. The instance SHALL freeze those substituted inputs. Compilations using the same full arguments and bound inputs SHALL select the same witness and associated bindings.

An explicit witness identity SHALL contain the selected satisfy declaration, canonical arguments, fixed priority, bound catalogue, and its relevant bound dependencies. A structural witness identity SHALL contain the constraint application, subject identity, bound catalogue, and canonical default/member/operation declarations forming its association table and requirements. A witness cache SHALL use these complete inputs. A cache entry SHALL become available after successful validation; an in-progress entry SHALL remain a dependency under the cycle rules.

A public boundary exposing an associated type or effect SHALL carry the selected witness dependency needed to interpret it. An image containing incompatible contracts for one canonical public identity SHALL report interface incompatibility. Duplicate-symbol merging SHALL require matching semantic identities. A separately revised catalogue SHALL be a distinct bound input; previously compiled definitions SHALL retain their bound selections until explicitly rebound through recompilation or a supported interface translation. Chapters 11 and 21 SHALL govern the selected compilation capability, and Chapter 29 SHALL encode these contracts when standardized contract export is selected.

### 7. Definition checking, recursion, and termination

A generic value-operation body SHALL establish its dependent operations throughout its declared parameter domain. Chapter 10's compile-time guards may refine that domain for a selected branch. A type mapping SHALL use Chapter 26's recipe rule: its definition establishes kinds and nondependent legality, and a required full application establishes the dependent result type under its concrete bindings. Definition-site name binding SHALL remain fixed in both cases.

An ordinary recursive function shall satisfy its signatures, lifecycle behavior, and effects; its execution may diverge unless it declares a stronger progress contract. Required compile-time recursion shall finish within the declared evaluation resources and satisfy the finite type and dependency rules.

Alias applications, partial and inline constructor normalization, witness formation, constraints, reflection, and generation SHALL resolve through completed acyclic requirements or a well-founded terminating evaluation. The checker SHALL count the visited finite kind nodes, substitutions, expanded argument positions, and proof work against their declared resources. A recursive kind descriptor SHALL remain a finite tree; a type-level computation may recur through separately declared mappings when its required evaluation completes. Recursive nominal records may use pointer or reference boundaries while retaining finite required value layouts. A resource limit shall produce the Resource exhausted outcome rather than a completed proof.

### 8. Effects, ownership, borrowing, and specialization

The selected instance shall retain its definition-site numerical, lifecycle, and effect policies. A callable witness shall satisfy the required receiver, return category, nonthrowing, borrow-source, escape, retention, consumption, and phase-specific effect contracts under Chapters 24 and 25.

A declared closed callable contract shall supply the interface evidence defined by Chapter 24; the implementation's body-checking obligations follow that chapter's selected validation mode. An open callable supplies only its conservative bound. Optional optimizer discoveries shall leave the published witness contract unchanged. A generic requiring a stronger bound shall obtain a supporting declared contract, established proof, or explicit conforming adapter.

Type substitution shall preserve the selected concrete type's independent copy, move, lifetime, destruction, abandonment, resource, and numerical contracts. A required unavailable allocator, format, or provider shall fail the corresponding capability check.

An asynchronous callable witness shall carry its independent admission and execution effects. Substitution shall preserve Chapter 25's phase order and Chapter 28's selected failure outlets.

### 9. Constant evaluation, reflection, and generation

Constraint selection shall use authored declarations and successfully committed generated declarations at the stages defined by [Chapter 23](#chapter-23-compile-time-generation). Reflection shall require Chapter 22's capability, query readiness, and access authority.

Explicit satisfy declarations SHALL remain authored catalogue entries. A permitted generation transaction may supply ordinary methods, aliases, generic declarations, and constraints within its typed-syntax capability. After commitment, those declarations may establish a structural witness or an authored conformance's requirements. The checker SHALL resolve the witness after its required declarations become complete and retain their committed identities in its dependency set.

Reflection and derivation shall use Chapter 23's single stage and grant model. A query depending on the querying transaction's uncommitted output shall fail the dependency check. A required constraint or generation budget failure shall use Section 3's resource outcome and preserve candidate-selection determinism.

### 10. ABI, identity, and separate compilation

An exported generic interface shall contain the declaration, kinds, requirements, witness identities, callable contracts, captured configuration, and definition material or precompiled-instance catalogue needed for its admitted uses. Consumers shall check those uses from that published contract.

Instance identity shall use Chapter 10 plus Chapter 26's constructor and associated-binding components. Emitted code sharing shall preserve Chapter 21's selected observations. Foreign boundaries shall use the verified wrappers or provider bindings in Chapters 09 and 20; compile-time constructor and witness identities shall remain compile-time entities.

An interface depending on private associated material SHALL publish the necessary reachable contract or expose a public opaque adapter. Identity matching SHALL use the bound semantic contracts. Standardized external contract export SHALL apply Chapter 29's representation and fingerprint rules when that capability is selected.

### 11. Required boundary behavior

| Case | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| A known nominal instance exposes the formal constructor argument position | Deduce the stored canonical constructor identity and validate its kind. |
| An omitted, independently undeduced typefn parameter has a declared default | Bind that constructor expression under its captured environment. |
| A required constructor argument has no explicit binding, direct deduction, or declared default | Report the missing argument. |
| An inline mapping binds a defaulted family position | Apply the default captured by that mapping and retain its dependency identity. |
| A prefix application binds part of a higher-order signature | Produce and check the finite residual kind. |
| T is independently deduced as i8 and i16 | Require one canonical deduction and report the mismatch. |
| Symbolic `N > 0` and `N >= 1` are compared for ordering | Retain distinct atoms and a tied constraint rank unless other standard evidence orders the entries. |
| A well-formed concrete declared constraint is false | Remove that candidate before ranking. |
| A candidate requirement has invalid nondependent syntax | Report the Malformed outcome. |
| Two matching explicit entries have different priorities | Visit the higher tier first; select its unique established entry or continue after an all-False tier. |
| Several entries are established in the first successful priority tier | Report ambiguity at the requiring use. |
| A higher tier succeeds while a lower dependent recipe would fail | Retain the selected witness and leave that lower dependent recipe unvisited. |
| A visited tier contains one Established and one Unestablished entry | Report the required-proof failure for that tier. |
| A visited condition reaches an Unestablished predicate and a lower tier has an applicable entry | Report the required-proof failure at the visited tier; retain the lower tier as unvisited. |
| An established False left operand guards a dependent predicate in a conjunction | Complete that condition as False through short-circuit evaluation, retaining the ordinary nondependent legality checks. |
| An established True left operand reaches an Unestablished predicate in a conjunction | Report the reached required-proof failure. |
| Every head-matching explicit entry is False and structural requirements hold | Select the structural fallback and produce GEN001. |
| No explicit head matches and structural requirements hold | Select the ordinary structural witness. |
| A cached structural witness carries all-False explicit provenance | Apply GEN001 under the current diagnostic configuration. |
| A selected body or association is invalid | Report the selected definition's error. |
| A required witness depends on its own unresolved selection | Apply the dependency-cycle rule. |
| Required solver resources are exhausted | Report the distinct compilation-resource outcome. |
| The caller imports another helper or conformance catalogue | Retain the generic definition's captured binding environment. |
| Optional analysis leaves an ordinary raw-pointer obligation unknown | Apply Chapter 24's ANOMALY policy while retaining required generic evidence. |
| A selected instance requires an unavailable format or ABI | Report its required capability. |

#### 11.1 Library author guidance: conditions with insufficient evidence

This subsection is informative. Sections 3 and 6.1 define the proof outcomes and selection transitions illustrated here. `P<T>`, `Q<T>`, and `Gate<T>` below are explanatory notation for already bound library requirements and their checking results. The tables illustrate the checker at the semantic level.

Consider a concrete subject S whose owner catalogue contains the following head-matching entries. All nondependent declaration checks have succeeded:

| Priority | Entry | Result of checking its condition and required contract at S |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 20 | A, using `P<S>` | Established. |
| 20 | B, using `Q<S>` | Unestablished: a required proposition lacks supporting evidence in its bound domain. |
| 0 | C | Would be Established if visited. |

Selection reaches priority 20 and reports B's required-proof failure. A's established condition does not complete the tier: the evidence has not established whether B is an applicable competitor. Entry C and structural fallback remain unvisited. A library author who intends C to handle an unsupported case needs the higher tier to reach established False outcomes for that case. The presence of C supplies an alternative implementation; its availability supplies no proof about B.

A concrete type argument fixes type identity while a required proposition may still depend on the declared evidence for a callable, associated projection, or generic domain. For example, an algorithm may require a closed callable effect or returned-borrow contract while its available callback interface exposes only an opaque or open bound. Section 8 requires a supporting declared contract, established proof, or conforming adapter for the stronger requirement. Merely obtaining the callback's ordinary parameter and result types supplies that ordinary signature. A rule establishing an incompatible structural contract produces False; the trace above specifically assumes an insufficient-evidence outcome under Section 3. These cases retain their separate classifications.

A useful condition shape is a decidable eligibility gate followed by the proof that the eligible branch needs. For the schematic condition `Gate<T> && Q<T>`, the existing short-circuit rules give:

| Checking at S | Condition result and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `Gate<S>` is established False | `Q<S>`'s dependent checking remains unvisited; the condition is False. Other entries in the tier still determine that tier's result. |
| `Gate<S>` is established True and `Q<S>` is Established | The condition succeeds; the remaining association and structural requirements are checked. |
| `Gate<S>` is established True and `Q<S>` is Unestablished | The reached proof fails and the visited tier reports ERROR. |

If replacing B's condition by the guarded form makes B False, A becomes the unique established entry in priority 20. If every head-matching entry in that tier becomes False, selection continues to priority 0. A gate such as a declared constant capability flag or a concrete core type predicate can delimit the intended domain. The gate itself needs an established result, and skipped dependent checking still preserves parsing and nondependent declaration legality.

Library authors can make these boundaries reviewable by documenting the supported subject domain and the source of each required fact. A callable's declared effect and lifetime contract can provide interface evidence; an adapter can expose the stronger contract that its implementation actually undertakes. Generic value-operation bodies establish their admitted domain at definition checking, with `if constexpr` supplying the branch refinement defined by Chapter 10. Those definition obligations precede concrete witness selection where applicable.

Review conditions using separate cases for supported input, established ineligibility, insufficient evidence, and exhausted compilation resources. A missing or incompatible structural operation has the False outcome defined in Section 3. An ordinary runtime-only Boolean call used where constant evaluation is required produces a required-evaluation error. Resource exhaustion retains its resource diagnostic. Each outcome keeps its defined classification, including the required-proof failure of an Unestablished proposition. The proof obligation applies to reached conditions and dependencies in visited tiers; lower tiers after a successful selection and short-circuited dependent branches keep their prescribed unvisited status.

### 12. Conformance requirements

An enabled implementation shall accept well-formed programs within its published capabilities and resource limits, produce deterministic candidate and witness selections, preserve required declaration evidence, and report ambiguity, malformed requirements, cycles, and resource exhaustion distinctly. The resulting native instances shall satisfy the same selected numeric, lifecycle, concurrency, effect, and ABI contracts as ordinary declarations.

---

<a id="chapter-28-error-recovery"></a>

## CPN26 Error and Recovery Specification

### 1. Scope and failure categories

This chapter SHALL govern language-exception formation, matching, retention, explicit capture, and recovery. The [core semantic model](#chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance) SHALL determine the identities and observable outcomes of error values, language exceptions, terminal failure, cancellation, and Whole transfer. Library calls SHALL use the invocation phases and failure routing in [Chapter 14](#chapter-14-standard-library).

Each specialized interface SHALL retain its declared outlet. A factory returning AllocationError SHALL deliver its own admitted allocation failure through that value; a user constructor called by the factory SHALL retain its separately declared exception and terminal effects. An exception-capture interface SHALL cover the interval stated in Section 8.

### 2. Error-value contracts

#### 2.1 Error identity and representation

An error value SHALL retain its nominal type and ordinary value semantics. `std::Result<T,E>` SHALL preserve E's canonical identity. A standard error record SHALL carry the discriminant, progress, ownership, and provider information required by its owning interface under Chapter 14's common representation contract.

Optional presentation text SHALL supplement that structured information. An owned presentation SHALL use its selected text/resource interface; a borrowed presentation SHALL use its declared borrow interval. User-supplied payload construction SHALL contribute its own effects. Failure during Err-payload construction SHALL follow that constructor's outlet while the intended Result remains unpublished.

#### 2.2 Result composition and explicit decisions

Result construction, observation, movement, and branch adapters SHALL follow [Chapter 16](#chapter-16-library-interfaces). Normal return of Err SHALL be normal return of a tagged value, including during constant evaluation. Nested Results SHALL preserve each layer until a selected adapter performs its stated composition.

A source `throw error;` SHALL construct a new exception payload under Section 4. A source return of `Err(error)` SHALL construct an ordinary error value. Each action SHALL preserve its own storage, lifetime, and continuation contract. Must-use acknowledgement and `discard(value);` SHALL follow Chapter 14; diagnostic policy SHALL follow Chapter 08.

#### 2.3 Locality of a checked outlet

A checked interface SHALL replace the outlet for the phases and error conditions identified by its contract. Callable and argument evaluation, parameter and result construction, callbacks, and retirement SHALL remain assigned to their declaring phase contracts. A checked divide SHALL report its own zero-divisor condition; a NumericTrap raised while computing its numerator SHALL select that earlier operation's terminal outlet before divide invocation.

### 3. Recovery guarantees and commitment

#### 3.1 Operation contracts

An operation SHALL identify the covered state, sources, aliases, resource effects, external progress, and observable phase transitions required by Chapter 14. Recovery SHALL use that published contract and the currently committed ownership state.

#### 3.2 Guarantee coverage

Unchanged, basic, and no-failure guarantees SHALL have their Chapter 14 meanings. A destination-only guarantee SHALL identify consumed sources and completed external effects separately. A failed constructor SHALL use the construction chapter's completed-subobject rollback on a continuing language-cleanup path. The selected terminal protocol SHALL govern paths entering terminal failure.

#### 3.3 Commitment and publication

Replacement commitment and returned-result publication SHALL follow Chapter 14. A retirement failure after replacement commitment SHALL preserve the committed representation and follow the selected retirement outlet. A catchable failure preventing result publication SHALL retire completed tentative output through its prescribed cleanup path. Successful publication of a Result SHALL publish its actual Ok or Err case.

#### 3.4 Retry and compensation

A selected retry policy SHALL resume only the phase and remaining prefix or suffix admitted by its contract. It SHALL account for already consumed arguments, released handles, and committed external progress in that continuation. An operation offering whole-operation replay SHALL specify the source states and external-effect contract that make replay valid.

Compensation SHALL be a separately contracted operation with its own progress and failure outcome. Static initialization SHALL use its declared compensation protocol. Other external-effect facilities SHALL use their selected domain compensation, where provided. A failed compensation SHALL expose the remaining committed state under that contract.

### 4. Forming a language exception

#### 4.1 Payload type and construction category

`throw expression;` SHALL require the language-exception capability. Its expression SHALL determine a payload type through existing auto value deduction: remove reference category and top-level qualification, preserve nested qualification, nominal identity, and array extent, and materialize abstract literals under their configured defaults. The type SHALL be a complete admitted object type with the required construction and final-disposal contracts.

Payload construction SHALL select copy construction for an lvalue, move construction for an expiring value, and final-destination construction for a same-type prvalue. Each selected construction SHALL satisfy its own availability constraints. A named lvalue SHALL retain its lvalue category. A direct prvalue payload SHALL require the operations actually used by direct construction.

The expression's static type SHALL determine a newly thrown payload. Throwing a base-reference value SHALL construct that static base value. Matching and retention of an existing record SHALL preserve its formed payload and dynamic identity.

A pointer payload SHALL contain the pointer value with its existing pointee borrow obligations. Pointer completeness SHALL depend on the pointer object type. Handler matching SHALL use that pointer-object identity under Section 5.

#### 4.2 Admission and operand evaluation

After determining the type, the selected exception provider SHALL admit record and final payload storage before runtime evaluation of the operand. The admitted storage SHALL satisfy the payload's alignment, lifetime, and selected record contract through the declared exception resource.

Admission success SHALL authorize exactly one operand evaluation and the selected final payload construction. Admission failure SHALL enter ExceptionInfrastructureFailure at that phase. The unstarted operand and payload SHALL remain in their pre-evaluation states. The intended primary SHALL commit only after payload formation succeeds.

If operand evaluation or payload construction raises another exception before commitment, that record SHALL propagate through its permitted route. Continuing cleanup SHALL roll back completed payload subobjects and release provisional record storage. The incomplete intended payload SHALL remain uncommitted. An immediate terminal outcome SHALL use the terminal protocol.

#### 4.3 The primary commitment point

Successful payload formation SHALL commit one propagation reference and a stable primary identity. Handler discovery SHALL precede cleanup of throw-expression temporaries and exited scopes for that propagation. The throw operand's full-expression temporaries SHALL participate in the ensuing cleanup.

In the aggregate profile, a later failure of a throw-expression temporary SHALL become a secondary of the committed primary. A destruction-boundary escape or uncaught propagation SHALL follow the boundary policy selected under Chapter 08 and Section 9.

A function that constructs the intended payload SHALL finish its own return protocol before its result can complete payload formation. Failure during that return protocol SHALL leave the intended record uncommitted and route its tentative output under the unpublished-result contract.

### 5. Handler matching and rethrow

#### 5.1 Primary type matching

Source handlers SHALL use these forms, with T naming an admitted payload view type:

```text
catch (T& value) { statements }
catch (const<T>& value) { statements }
catch aggregate (view) { statements }
catch (...) { statements }
```

The aggregate form SHALL bind a read-only ExceptionAggregate view of the handled record.

A typed handler SHALL bind an lvalue-reference view of the primary payload. Its object type SHALL match the canonical payload type or an accessible, unambiguous base subobject. A shared virtual base SHALL identify one subobject; multiple distinct candidate base subobjects SHALL fail the uniqueness condition.

The view's qualification SHALL determine its mutation permission. Matching SHALL use exact canonical identity or the admitted base relationship, with the existing payload retained in place. A pointer payload SHALL bind through an lvalue reference to its exact pointer-object type. Access and canonical identity SHALL follow the type and module rules.

Within the nearest eligible handler set, selection SHALL consider matching primary handlers in source order, aggregate-view handlers in source order next, and catch-all last. Secondary records SHALL remain observation data of the selected aggregate. A typed handler for a user-thrown ExceptionAggregate payload SHALL retain its ordinary typed-handler identity.

An exception raised from a handler body SHALL search eligible surrounding handler sets. A nested try within that body SHALL establish its own local set.

#### 5.2 Active handler context

Handler entry SHALL establish an active record context through completion of its exit protocol, including handler-local cleanup. Exit SHALL restore the previously active context. A propagating record SHALL become a handled record when its handler is entered.

The context SHALL belong to the logical execution. An async handler SHALL retain it across admitted suspension and worker migration. A new Task, thread, or independent callback SHALL begin with its own handler context, including on an inline executor. A synchronous helper SHALL use its caller's context until it crosses a declared independent entry.

#### 5.3 Bare rethrow and a new throw

`throw;` SHALL resolve the innermost active handler context and acquire a propagation reference to that record. It SHALL preserve primary identity and the secondary sequence. Each active handler SHALL retain its lifetime reference until its exit protocol completes. A valid synchronous helper SHALL resolve the same logical context.

A nested try that catches this rethrow SHALL preserve the still-active outer handler's payload view and record lifetime. A propagation exiting that outer handler SHALL release its reference at the ordinary exit point. Physical bookkeeping SHALL obey the transformation model while preserving these lifetimes.

A valid active context SHALL select identity-preserving propagation. Dynamic absence SHALL select ContractTrap before record access. A proved invalid context and an admitted unproved context obligation SHALL receive their canonical Chapter 08 diagnostics.

`throw expression;` SHALL follow Section 4 and create a new primary after formation. For `throw caught;`, the static expression type and category SHALL select the new payload. A program requiring a relation to the handled record SHALL retain that earlier record explicitly.

### 6. Source-level retained exception ownership

#### 6.1 Module and ABI identities

The optional module std.error SHALL expose Sections 6–8 when language exceptions and a compatible exception provider are selected. Actual interface uses SHALL contribute their provider requirements to the resolved capability record under Chapter 14.

`std::error::ExceptionHandle` SHALL own one retained record reference or have the empty state. The originating provider SHALL own payload storage. The ExceptionRef transport in [Chapter 08](#chapter-08-runtime-configuration) SHALL retain its declared two-pointer ABI; acquisition of source ownership SHALL occur through a retain or adopt operation.

ExceptionAggregate SHALL be the read-only observation view of the exception facility. A borrowed view SHALL use its handler's or owner's reference lifetime. A retained ABI result SHALL be adopted exactly once into its source-level ExceptionHandle.

#### 6.2 Handle state and operations

The following schemas SHALL use the existing value and receiver rules. Observers SHALL use read-only receivers. The handle's construction and assignment capabilities SHALL be exactly the following catalogue.

| Operation | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `ExceptionHandle()` | Construct an empty handle. |
| Move construction | Transfer the single reference and empty the source. |
| Move assignment | Require an empty destination; self-move preserves state. Transfer the source reference and empty the source. A nonempty distinct destination selects ContractTrap. |
| `bool has_value()` | Return whether the handle owns one reference. |
| `ExceptionHandle retain()` | Acquire and return one additional owner for a nonempty handle; return empty for an empty handle. |
| `ExceptionAggregate aggregate()` | Return the borrowed view of a nonempty record; select ContractTrap for an empty handle. |
| `void reset() noexcept` | Empty the handle, then release its previously owned reference once; preserve empty state when already empty. |
| Destructor | Perform reset through the final-disposal boundary. |

Construction, movement, retention, reset, and observation SHALL perform record-reference bookkeeping using the existing record storage. Bookkeeping success SHALL deliver its specified state transition; impossible bookkeeping SHALL enter ExceptionInfrastructureFailure. Final release SHALL invoke the selected payload finalizer and release record storage. The finalizer SHALL retain its declared resource, I/O, and internally handled exception effects. An exception escaping payload disposal or provider release SHALL enter ExceptionDisposalFailure.

Reset SHALL publish the empty handle state before final release so reentrant observation of that handle sees empty. Other reentrant accesses SHALL satisfy the payload's current lifetime state. Provider, allocator, matching descriptors, finalizer code, and required code images SHALL remain alive through every outstanding reference and active operation under Chapter 14's retention contract.

#### 6.3 Aggregate observation ownership

ExceptionAggregate SHALL expose the following read-only source catalogue. u64 counting and indexing SHALL require the enabled u64 capability of the selected exception observation contract.

| Operation | Result and ownership |
| --- | --- |
| `const<void>* identity()` | Opaque record identity stable through the retained record lifetime. |
| `const<void>* primary_type()` | Borrowed canonical dynamic type-descriptor pointer. |
| `const<T>* primary_as<T>()` | Borrowed matching primary/base view, or null under Section 5's matching relation. |
| `u64 secondary_count()` | Count of retained secondary records. |
| `ExceptionHandle secondary(u64 index)` | Adopt one retained reference to the selected secondary; invalid indexing selects NumericTrap. |
| `Result<ExceptionHandle,ExceptionAccessError> try_secondary(u64 index)` | Adopt one selected reference on success; return the bounded payloadless InvalidIndex on failure with the source reference set unchanged. |
| `u64 omitted_count()` | Known omitted-secondary count, saturating at maximum u64. |
| `bool truncated()` | True when a secondary was omitted or the omission counter saturated. |
| `ExceptionHandle retain()` | Acquire one additional owner of this record. |

Identity SHALL remain stable while the retained record is alive. A primary-type descriptor SHALL use Chapter 08's canonical identity and matching protocol for cross-module equivalence. Descriptor pointer values SHALL designate the borrowed local transport descriptor; comparison of payload types SHALL use that canonical protocol. Each returned secondary owner SHALL permit a read-only aggregate view through aggregate().

The exception ABI release operation SHALL discharge an owned reference. A source owner SHALL discharge its reference through reset, destruction, or a declared raw-ABI transfer. A borrowed catch view SHALL observe through the handler-owned reference. Source ownership acquisition SHALL use the catalogue in this chapter and the compatible raw-ABI adoption contract.

`primary_as<T>()` SHALL return a read-only pointer to an exact or admitted base payload view, and null for a mismatched type. The pointer SHALL borrow from the retained owner or active handler supplying the view. Matching SHALL use Section 5's type relation.

#### 6.4 Concurrent references and aggregate metadata

A record provider supporting multiple execution agents SHALL synchronize reference acquisition/release, secondary publication, and observation. Sequenced cleanup observations SHALL preserve their order. Concurrent append operations SHALL have one recorded order consistent with existing ordering relations; otherwise the provider SHALL choose that order.

Each count, flag, and indexed-secondary observer SHALL observe a valid published state. Separate calls SHALL be separate observations. Entries SHALL remain retained through the record's lifetime. Concurrent cycle validation and publication SHALL preserve an acyclic secondary-retention graph. An append exceeding the provider's validation budget SHALL follow the existing omission and truncation rule. User payload references SHALL retain their ordinary ownership and cycle-management contract.

Mutable primary-payload access SHALL follow the memory model and its selected synchronization. Borrowed payload resources SHALL retain their ordinary lifetime contract when records are shared or raised on another agent.

### 7. Current record and identity-preserving raise

The enabled std.error module SHALL provide:

```cpn
namespace std {
    namespace error {
        declare Option<ExceptionHandle> current_exception() noexcept;
        declare never raise(const<ExceptionHandle>& record);
    }
}
```

`current_exception()` SHALL return None for an empty active-handler context. Otherwise it SHALL retain the innermost handled record once and return Some of its owning handle.

`raise(record)` SHALL require a live nonempty handle, acquire a propagation reference, and propagate the same record while the source handle keeps its reference. Primary identity, dynamic payload type, and retained secondaries SHALL remain preserved. Permitted subsequent cleanup SHALL append secondaries under its selected profile. Raising an empty handle SHALL select ContractTrap before propagation.

A retained record SHALL remain raisable after its original handler exits while its provider and code obligations remain satisfied. Raising from a handler or another agent SHALL use normal eligible-handler search, logical entry boundaries, and cycle/exhaustion rules. Bare rethrow SHALL obtain its source from the active context; raise SHALL obtain its source from the supplied owner. Each SHALL acquire a propagation reference while preserving still-live source owners.

### 8. Explicit exception capture

#### 8.1 `attempt` contract

`std::error::attempt<T>(callable)` SHALL invoke a synchronous nullary callable and return `std::Result<T,std::error::ExceptionHandle>`. T SHALL be a complete admitted object type or void, and the callable result SHALL be exactly T. A reference result SHALL use an explicit std::Ref wrapper.

The parameter SHALL be a forwarding borrow and the adapter SHALL invoke it exactly once with the supplied category. The callable SHALL remain owned by its existing owner.
