<a id="chapter-30-reference-target-bindings"></a>

## CPN26 Reference Native Target Bindings Specification

### 1. Complete baseline contracts

This chapter defines two complete baseline bindings: `cpn.ref.linux-x86_64.core.v1` and `cpn.ref.windows-x86_64.core.v1`. They instantiate the corresponding [target families](#chapter-20-target-abi-profiles) with fixed interface subsets and explicit runtime absence. They are conformance contracts, not a claim that an existing CPN26 compiler or a named foreign toolchain has been tested.

The bindings support ordinary native relocatable objects, C scalar/pointer calls, verified plain C records, and callbacks. A C++ translation unit can consume their generated C interface under `extern "C"`. The Linux binding additionally supports the limited direct C++ symbol subset in Section 4. The supported feature subset shall be exactly the positive claims in its profile record. Additional direct C++ features shall use a separately versioned binding.

Each baseline shall use the explicit absent-runtime bindings in its record for the native CPN26 component. The CPN26 component/configuration domain selecting it shall set `exceptions.language = false` and use serial native-domain initialization. A capability requiring a missing runtime creates an explicit derived profile with its own complete dependency contract; it does not change the meaning of the baseline identifier. These constraints select a low-level conformance subset rather than changing the language's optional exception, concurrency, or allocation facilities.

All options in the baseline descriptor are fixed. A provider may implement another profile, including a superset, under a distinct identity. Shared boundaries compare their relevant contracts, so an extended image may still use these exact C-compatible function/record interfaces. A different private runtime does not by itself invalidate an unchanged C boundary.

#### 1.1 Normative platform references

The following references supply only their specified platform rules. A later webpage edit does not automatically revise a CPN26 profile. The named edition and this chapter's subset/options govern. An implementation shall preserve the identified reference edition or equivalent versioned contract in its provider evidence.

| Reference ID | Edition and normative use |
| --- | --- |
| `sysv-amd64-2018` | [System V AMD64 psABI, Version 1.0, January 28, 2018](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/hjl-tools/x86-psabi/x86-64-psABI-1.0.pdf), LP64 portions of Sections 3 and 4 and Linux conventions relevant to the selected object subset. |
| `itanium-1.86` | [Itanium C++ ABI, revision 1.86](https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/cxxabi-1.86.html), Section 5.1 external-name rules restricted by Section 4 below. |
| `ms-x64-call-2025` | [Microsoft x64 calling convention](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/x64-calling-convention?view=msvc-170), documented revision dated March 19, 2025; default fixed-prototype, scalar/record, callback and supported variadic calls. |
| `ms-x64-layout-2025` | [Microsoft x64 software conventions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/x64-software-conventions?view=msvc-170), documented revision dated March 28, 2025; scalar and ordinary record layout. |
| `ms-pe-coff-2026` | [Microsoft PE/COFF format](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/debug/pe-format), revision displayed September 10, 2026; AMD64 relocatable COFF sections, symbols, relocations and procedure-data transport. |
| `ms-x64-unwind1` | [Microsoft x64 exception-handling data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/exception-handling-x64?view=msvc-170), `RUNTIME_FUNCTION` and version-1 `UNWIND_INFO` forms without language handlers. |

The Linux call classifier uses the pinned psABI's complete classification for the supported types, including hidden result storage, register exhaustion, stack alignment, and variadic metadata. CPN26 evaluation order still governs expression evaluation before ABI marshalling. No change to source integer-promotion rules follows from the foreign variadic boundary.

The Windows classifier uses the default Microsoft x64 convention: its four parameter positions, prescribed integer/floating registers, caller shadow store, and indirect record rules. It does not use a System V red zone. Nonleaf frames use required `.pdata`/`.xdata` unwind metadata even though CPN26 language exceptions and a foreign language-unwind bridge are disabled. Metadata permitting a debugger to recover a frame is not permission to bypass its lifetime contract.

### 2. Common scalar, record, and ownership subset

Both profiles use eight-bit bytes, little-endian object representation, flat 64-bit object and function pointers, one default address space, and 16-byte call-stack alignment. A null object or function pointer has zero representation in these bindings. This representation fact does not make arbitrary integers valid pointers or erase pointer lifetime/generation rules. Function pointers and object pointers remain distinct source types.

The scalar descriptor arrays in Section 6 give exact storage and alignment. Signed foreign integers use two's complement. Foreign Boolean objects use one byte and canonical false/true values 0/1. `ffi::c_char` is signed; signed-char and unsigned-char identities remain distinct. The `int`, `long`, and `long long` foreign identities remain distinct even when widths coincide. [Microsoft's data-type contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/cpp/data-type-ranges?view=msvc-170) additionally binds its long-double representation to binary64 and wide character to unsigned 16-bit storage. The Linux profile binds long double to the psABI's x87 extended representation in its 16-byte storage slot; its padding is not value data.

A supported direct C record shall be nonempty, use natural packing/alignment and trivial copy/destruction, and contain supported scalar/pointer fields, fixed nonzero arrays of those fields, or recursively supported records. The profile's record-layout capability consists exactly of this grammar. Additional layouts shall use a separately declared capability. Ordinary native CPN26 records use their enabled language features.

Every crossing record supplies field offsets, total size/alignment, type identities, and its by-value classification in its binding contract. Its generated C17 header uses the same transport declarations and static size/offset assertions where expressible, with C++ `extern "C"` guards. Assertions do not establish an ownership or exception contract; the descriptor carries those obligations separately. Array members keep exact extents. A scalar-only C function need not carry record metadata it does not use.

A foreign enumeration shall use an explicit integer-transport wrapper with its declared enum-domain validation. `wchar_t` storage is bound for explicitly imported declarations but does not change CPN26's Unicode-scalar `char` identity. Native `usize`/`isize` keep their own family identity; they are not automatic aliases for foreign `size_t`/`ptrdiff_t`.

Callbacks use the same supported C call contract, with explicit context borrowing and retention lifetime. Stateful callback transport shall use the declared context parameter or an explicit adapter. Varargs require a fixed prototype and admit only the profile's supported scalar/pointer variadic transports, with the required foreign default promotions. Other variadic transports shall use a profile declaring their call classification.

A borrowed pointer carries no release authority. An owning pointer transport includes explicit destroy/release callbacks or a named compatible allocator contract. There is no implicit libc `free`, C++ `delete`, or cross-CRT allocation compatibility. A native wrapper cannot independently destroy the members of a foreign object already destroyed by its foreign complete destructor. Ordinary C++ objects can be used through an opaque C interface with its own explicit ownership/effect contract without claiming direct class-layout support.

### 3. Object files and support closure

The Linux binding emits ELF64 relocatable objects with `EM_X86_64`; the Windows binding emits ordinary AMD64 COFF relocatable objects with machine identifier `0x8664`. Neither object is only compiler IR, and neither requires CPN26-specific LTO to link. Reference-compatible C symbols use their exact ASCII source name without a leading underscore. Export/import visibility and any final shared-image export list are explicit binding inputs.

The baseline linker input shall consist of relocatable objects with single-owner definitions and explicit dependencies. Archive extraction shall use an independently declared tool contract. Generic/inline emissions shall use one definition owner or a separately bound COMDAT capability.

The Linux position model is small PIC under the pinned AMD64 relocation rules. Windows uses the standard AMD64 COFF position/relocation model, without claiming that COFF and ELF relocations are interchangeable. Each emitted relocation shall belong to its selected target contract. Native TLS, vector calling conventions, multiversioning, and executable trampolines shall use an extended profile declaring their additional support. A required compiler helper not implemented inside the object becomes an explicit additional dependency and is unavailable until a compatible derived binding selects it.

An admitted cross-frame control transfer shall satisfy the baseline's non-unwinding lifetime boundary. The baseline admits a foreign call or callback only when its non-unwinding requirement is established by verified evidence or by a verified adapter that terminates or translates failure on its originating side before an unwind enters a CPN26 frame. An admitted assertion shall satisfy the originating-side terminal boundary required by Chapter 09. If that obligation requires a guard unavailable in this baseline, direct binding is `ERROR`; an explicitly supported guarded or derived binding is required. Other permitted unproved programmer obligations retain their ordinary ANOMALY rules. Numeric and contract terminal outlets remain noncatchable and non-unwinding. The baseline terminal operation emits an x86 `UD2` terminal site; no native code resumes after it. A host handler may report or terminate the image, but resuming a failed CPN26 operation is not a supported recovery protocol.

A composed image may contain separately contracted C/C++ components and their explicit CRT, exception-runtime, and library dependencies. Those remain foreign component obligations; they do not create an implicit CPN26 runtime requirement or change an unchanged supported C boundary. The absence of native-component CRT support is exact. Its emitted support references shall be exactly the explicit dependency closure of that binding. An explicitly selected diagnostic/support adapter may provide reporting through a derived dependency contract. The general language's Debug/Release semantics still apply to the capabilities actually enabled; this runtime-free baseline does not promise debug aggregation for disabled language exceptions.

#### 3.1 Native numerical provider binding

The ABI profile shall determine object format, transport, instruction availability, and support dependencies. Ordinary numerical execution shall additionally bind the `numeric.native` capability described in Chapter 29. That capability shall publish Native integer domain outcomes, floating controls/clobber, NaN/subnormal behavior, and permitted transformations or approximations for the supported widths/formats. A Native lowering shall use the ABI profile's declared instruction set and dependency closure. A stronger numerical operation shall bind the corresponding checked/reporting/accuracy capability. Thus a foreign transport profile and a numerical execution profile have separate, explicit identities.

### 4. Linux direct C++ symbol subset

The Linux baseline's `cpp_symbol` claim covers C++03 non-template free functions with externally linked ASCII identifiers in ordinary namespaces. Parameter and return types are the supported foreign scalar/pointer types, or lvalue references to those types, with ordinary cv qualification. Function overloads use their actual imported foreign nominal types and the pinned Itanium external-name grammar. The direct symbol subset shall consist exactly of this free-function and type grammar.

A reference parameter has the selected ABI's reference transport and a live referent obligation. It does not become a nullable optional reference. Return types and all effect/ownership conditions remain part of the binding even where the external name does not encode them. An imported declaration shall match those conditions independently of successful symbol lookup.

For example, a global foreign `int add(int,int)` has external name `_Z3addii`, while global foreign `long add(long,long)` has `_Z3addll`. The same bit width of a native CPN26 type is insufficient to choose either foreign overload. The descriptor names the actual foreign declarations and their non-unwinding contract.

The Linux direct C++ claim shall cover the symbol subset above. A separately verified adapter may call such facilities on its foreign side and expose a supported non-unwinding boundary. Its required compiler, runtime, library ABI switches, and release operations are explicit additional contracts.

### 5. Explicit static-domain entry

A baseline image with dynamic native static objects shall expose two C entry points with prototypes `void start(void)` and `void stop(void)`. These are schematic names; the resolved link contract shall bind their actual unique external symbols. A selected standard export shall place them in `link_requirements`. The explicit host startup/shutdown caller shall own that domain.

The host calls `start` exactly once before any exported operation requiring domain readiness, and calls `stop` exactly once after those operations and retained callbacks cease. The state transition is `Cold -> Starting -> Ready -> Stopping -> Stopped`. Reentry, a second start/stop, start after stop, and access before readiness violate the explicit domain contract. A proven invalid transition is `ERROR`; an unproved host obligation is `ANOMALY`, with the existing contract-failure rule at a validated boundary.

Startup is serial in the language's logical rank order, and shutdown uses reverse logical rank. Constant objects with destruction obligations participate in the same registry. A terminal initializer failure does not return success or call a hidden catch-all collector. There is no automatic restart after partial startup. Domain storage and registration work are statically owned by the image, with no hidden heap allocation. An object with no dynamic startup or shutdown obligation creates no entry point or registry solely to satisfy this section.

The host retains the image and all required code while any exported reference, callback, object destructor, or disposal operation depends on it. Unloading an image cannot discharge live obligations by discarding its code. A richer dynamic loader, parallel startup scheduler, or CRT integration uses a separately declared provider contract.

### 6. Normative profile records

The following reference JSON records instantiate the [public ABI schema](#chapter-29-public-contract-schemas). A claim to a reference target shall implement its stated target facts. An implementation may retain those facts internally; producing these public records and their SHA-256 identities shall follow a selected `tooling.contract_export` request. Contract strings such as `core.records.v1` refer to the exact clauses of this chapter. `none` means intentionally unsupported or absent. Each complete reference document includes its reference list. Pretty-printing aids reading; canonical encoding determines the displayed fingerprint.

`options` has exactly these fields for these profiles: `plain_char` (`signed`), `packing` (`natural`), `short_enums` (`false`), `foreign_enums` (`false`), `vector_abi` (`false`), `record_varargs` (`false`), `language_exceptions` (`false`), `static_schedule` (`serial`), `crt_libraries` (empty set), and `cxx_library` (`none`). Their values cannot be overridden while retaining the profile identifier.

### 7. Boundary compatibility and diagnostic rules

A provider claiming either baseline shall implement exactly its selected feature subset and fixed options. Packing, long-double format, C++ ABI, CRT, and exception support shall use the record's bound values. Producer identity/version and actual selected linker/tool inputs are recorded in build context; conformance is to the versioned target contract, not equality of compiler brand names.

A function or record imported from C/C++ is directly usable only when its own binding contract matches the supported subset. A compatible machine architecture alone is insufficient. A verified adapter may explicitly translate to a supported interface with its own ownership and failure contract. Unsupported requested class/RTTI/exception features produce `ERROR` for direct use; an unproved obligation expressly permitted by the language produces `ANOMALY` and is never represented as verified compatibility.

CPN26 floating result/status rules, checked integer arithmetic, destruction responsibilities, and explicit terminal behavior remain in force inside native functions. Their ABI marshalling shall preserve required observable representations, including signaling NaNs where an inspection contract requires it. A foreign function's internal arithmetic follows its declared foreign contract; this profile does not retrofit CPN26 numerical guarantees onto arbitrary C or C++ code.

---

<a id="chapter-31-units-interfaces"></a>

## CPN26 Quantity and Affine Point Interfaces Specification

### 1. Scope and identity

The optional std.units module supplies the following names in namespace std::units. Signature tables instantiate the ordinary generic grammar: descriptors are types, and numerical metadata parameters are admitted integer constants. [Chapter 04](#chapter-04-numeric-integration) owns numerical projection, status, and failure; the [core model](#chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance) owns execution and object lifetime.

Descriptors shall determine static type identity. Quantity and Point shall store one representation object and use that object's construction, ownership, and operation contracts. Ordinary arithmetic inherits the selected Rep policy, including Native Release. Named conversions below select their stronger projection contracts explicitly.

### 2. Canonical descriptors

#### 2.1 Dimensions

`Dimensionless` denotes an empty dimension. `Axis<Tag>` denotes exponent one of the nominal type Tag. Tag is a complete nominal object type; its exported type identity, not its fields, spelling, or layout, identifies the axis. Aliases of one Tag identify the same axis. Different nominal tags remain different even when both are empty records.

`ProductDimension<A,B>`, `QuotientDimension<A,B>`, and `PowerDimension<A,Exponent>` are type aliases forming the product, quotient, and integer power of admitted dimension descriptors. Exponent is a `const i32` parameter. Their canonical identity is the finite map from axis identity to nonzero i32 exponent: products add exponents, quotients subtract, powers multiply, and zero entries disappear. Equivalent maps denote one type regardless of expression order. Required metadata evaluation shall diagnose ERROR for an unrepresentable exponent.

The following empty tag types and dimension aliases are standard. Each dimension alias means Axis of its row's tag; the canonical unit fixes the interpretation of Scale.

| Tag | Dimension alias | Canonical unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LengthTag` | `LengthDimension` | metre |
| `MassTag` | `MassDimension` | kilogram |
| `TimeTag` | `TimeDimension` | second |
| `ElectricCurrentTag` | `ElectricCurrentDimension` | ampere |
| `TemperatureTag` | `TemperatureDimension` | kelvin |
| `AmountTag` | `AmountDimension` | mole |
| `LuminousIntensityTag` | `LuminousIntensityDimension` | candela |
| `AngleTag` | `AngleDimension` | radian |
| `InformationTag` | `InformationDimension` | bit |

Angle and information shall retain their axis identities. Applications may supply nominal currency or domain tags through Axis. Dimension multiplication shall apply this algebra; exchange rates and other domain conversions require their own operation contracts.

#### 2.2 Ratios and scales

`Ratio<N,D>` is a canonical descriptor alias whose parameters are `const i64 N` and `const u64 D`. D shall be positive. It reduces N/D by the mathematical greatest common divisor, retaining the numerator sign and a positive denominator; zero canonicalizes to 0/1. Equal reduced fractions denote the same descriptor type. The descriptor exposes public associated constants `i64 numerator` and `u64 denominator`. Computing the magnitude of i64.MIN for reduction is mathematical metadata evaluation, not an overflowing signed negation.

`Scale<N,D>` aliases Ratio<N,D> but rejects N equal to zero. `Offset<N,D>` aliases Ratio<N,D> without that restriction. `ProductScale<A,B>` and `QuotientScale<A,B>` require nonzero ratio descriptors, compute their exact product or quotient, reduce it, and produce the canonical scale type. Required metadata evaluation shall use the exact reduced result and diagnose ERROR when its numerator or denominator exceeds the declared domain.

`UnitScale`, `PercentScale`, `NanosecondScale`, `BitScale`, and `ByteScale` alias respectively Scale<1,1>, Scale<1,100>, Scale<1,1000000000>, Scale<1,1>, and Scale<8,1>. The bit/byte aliases apply to InformationDimension; a scalar ratio does not itself acquire that dimension. These descriptor facilities shall require their stated i32/i64/u64 constant-parameter capabilities.

#### 2.3 Affine origins

`Origin<D,Frame,O>` is a descriptor type with a canonical dimension D, a complete nominal frame type Frame, and an Offset descriptor O. Its public nested type aliases `Dimension`, `FrameType`, and `OffsetType` name those arguments. Its offset is measured in D's canonical unit relative to that frame's zero. `ZeroOrigin<D,Frame>` aliases Origin<D,Frame,Offset<0,1>>. Equal canonical arguments produce the same origin identity.

Origin conversion shall require identical dimension and frame identities. Distinct frames remain distinct even when their offsets match. Clock correlation, currency exchange, physical calibration, and conversion to std::time::Instant<Clock> shall use their own explicit interfaces.

### 3. Construction, access, and lifetime

`Quantity<D,Rep,S>` requires a canonical dimension D, a nonzero scale S, and a complete nonreference object type Rep. `Point<D,Rep,S,O>` additionally requires an Origin whose dimension is D. Both expose public nested type aliases `Dimension`, `Representation`, and `ScaleType`; Point additionally exposes `OriginType`. They name the canonical supplied arguments. Each wrapper shall construct its sole representation subobject in place; its foreign ABI transport uses its declared wrapper binding.

| Operation on either wrapper | Required contract |
| --- | --- |
| Direct construction from `args...` | Directly construct Rep from the individually forwarded arguments, evaluated once under ordinary construction rules. Available exactly when that Rep construction is available. |
| Default construction | Use the zero-argument Rep construction and its typed default value/resource contract. |
| Same-type copy/move construction | Copy/move the representation with its ordinary requirements, effects, and moved-from state. |
| Same-type copy/move assignment | Apply the corresponding Rep assignment when available; preserve its failure and self-assignment contract. |
| `representation()` on mutable receiver | `Rep&`, borrowing the existing representation subobject. |
| `representation()` on read-only receiver | `const<Rep>&`, with the same borrow origin. |
| Destruction | Destroy the representation exactly once under the selected lifecycle profile. |

Same-type copy/move construction shall select its dedicated operation. A single argument of another wrapper type is admitted by forwarding exactly when that type is Rep, including an explicitly nested representation. Other metadata changes shall use the named conversion catalogue. Explicit extraction followed by construction asserts the caller's chosen new interpretation.

Representation access shall borrow the existing subobject for its lifetime. Mutation changes its stored value under the same static metadata. Copying an allocating Rep shall use that representation's resource contract. Construction and failure shall follow the core lifecycle rules for the one subobject.

### 4. Arithmetic and comparisons

An overload shall require the corresponding Rep operation with exactly Rep as its value result, or bool for a comparison. It shall invoke that operation once under the source order and selected numerical contract. A Native representation operation retains its native value/fault behavior and unobserved events; an explicitly observed/Checked representation operation retains its own guarantees. Different representations require explicit unification.

| Operands and operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Quantity<D,Rep,S>` plus/minus the same type | The same Quantity type. |
| Unary plus/minus of a Quantity | The same type, using the corresponding Rep operation. |
| `Quantity<A,Rep,SA>` multiplied by `Quantity<B,Rep,SB>` | Quantity<ProductDimension<A,B>,Rep,ProductScale<SA,SB>>. |
| Those quantities divided | Quantity<QuotientDimension<A,B>,Rep,QuotientScale<SA,SB>>. |
| `Point<D,Rep,S,O>` minus the same Point type | Quantity<D,Rep,S>. |
| That Point plus/minus Quantity<D,Rep,S> | The same Point type. Quantity plus Point has the corresponding addition overload. |
| Equality/inequality of identical wrapper types | The corresponding representation comparison. |
| Ordered comparison of identical wrapper types | The representation comparison, with operands reversed when S is negative. |

The table defines the standard overload set. Comparisons shall use Rep's declared comparison behavior and require its corresponding overload. Integer division, overflow, and floating rounding occur at the Rep operation boundaries. Required metadata shall be representable before admission of the resulting type.

### 5. Named conversions

#### 5.1 Catalogue and admissibility

The following functions use the canonical `std::numeric::NumericResult`, `NumericStatus`, `NumericErrorCode`, and `RoundingMode`. Destination and Source are complete Quantity types of the same dimension, or complete Point types of the same dimension and frame. Quantity and Point shall each convert within their own wrapper family. Scale and origin offset may differ.

The baseline source representations are enabled fixed integers and scalar IEEE binary/fixed-decimal floats. Exact destinations may use either of those families. Checked destinations also admit both families; Saturating destinations are fixed integers. Other Rep families may supply explicit conversion extensions publishing their signatures, resources, and projection semantics.

| Function | Result and projection |
| --- | --- |
| `convert_exact<Destination>(const<Source>& source)` | NumericResult<Destination>; finite representability probe, no rounding. |
| `convert_checked<Destination>(const<Source>& source,RoundingMode rounding)` | NumericResult<Destination>; one final rounded projection with the numeric Checked acceptance rule. |
| `convert_saturating<Destination>(const<Source>& source,RoundingMode rounding)` | NumericResult<Destination>; selected integer rounding followed by clamping. |

The caller shall supply every argument and handle the must-use NumericResult. Each named conversion shall retain its defined acceptance predicate across execution presets.

#### 5.2 Exact transformed value

Let x be the actual source representation value, Ss/St the source/destination scales, and Os/Ot their origin offsets. Quantity conversion computes the exact mathematical target coefficient `y = x * Ss / St`. Point conversion computes `y = (x * Ss + Os - Ot) / St`. The operation projects y once to the destination Rep, then directly constructs Destination from that projected representation.

An encoded floating source contributes its actual value. The implementation shall realize the exact affine formula and one destination projection through the selected bounded capability. Admission requires support for the enabled source/destination formats and metadata; classification shall use the final mathematical projection, independently of avoidable intermediate overflow.

For a floating destination, exact zero retains the source floating zero sign multiplied by the scale ratio's sign when the net offset is zero. Other exact cancellations to zero produce positive zero. Rounding a nonzero negative y to floating zero retains its negative sign. Numerical conversion does not promise decimal cohort or other nonnumeric representation preservation.

#### 5.3 Failure and status

The implementation shall apply Chapter 04's corresponding Exact, Checked, or Saturating destination projection to y. Exact probes preserve FP status; Checked floating projection uses gradual subnormals and its local events; integer projection uses its CPN26 status. Their acceptance predicates and delivery remain independent of ambient arithmetic trap/error masks.

Exact and Checked shall reject a nonfinite source as NonFinite through representation inspection that preserves the signaling class and FP status. Saturating integer conversion shall reject NaN as NonFinite and map infinity to the destination bound after applying the scale ratio's sign. This catalogue sets wrapped and payload_changed false and otherwise uses the selected projection's canonical status fields.

Success shall directly construct Destination from the projected representation and return it with local status. Failure shall return Err without a Destination payload and preserve the source. Argument evaluation and independent user effects retain their core execution boundaries.

<a id="chapter-32-numeric-resource-interfaces"></a>

## CPN26 Numeric Resource Interfaces Specification

### 1. Scope and identities

Numeric resource operations SHALL apply the [common library model](#chapter-14-standard-library), [core operational model](#chapter-21-abstract-machine-conformance), and existing BigInt value contracts. This chapter specifies quota geometry, plan binding, temporary epochs, and persistent ownership transfer.

New resource names SHALL belong to std::numeric. BigInt and NumericResult SHALL retain their canonical numeric identities; ResourceRef, AllocatorRef, ResourceError, and Span SHALL use std::mem identities, and Option/Result their std identities. Policy copying SHALL preserve its borrowing terms and selected resource domain. These explicitly selected quota and temporary operations SHALL retain their defined outcomes in Native and observed execution alike.

### 2. Geometry and quota policies

`AllocationShape` SHALL contain usize bytes and usize alignment, with positive provider-supported alignment. GeometryIdentity SHALL be an opaque equality-comparable identity of one versioned reservation/charge contract. A provider factory or exported descriptor SHALL supply nonempty GeometryRef as an immutable copyable borrow of that contract.

| GeometryRef operation | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `identity() -> GeometryIdentity` | Observe the complete versioned identity. |
| `allocator() -> AllocatorRef` | Borrow the allocator contract for which this geometry is valid. |
| `supports(AllocationShape shape) -> bool` | Whether this size/alignment belongs to the geometry. |
| `charge(AllocationShape shape) -> NumericResult<usize>` | Exact retained charge, including alignment rounding and required allocation metadata. |
| `reservation_charge(usize capacity) -> NumericResult<usize>` | Exact backing and control charge for a reservation of that capacity. |
| `guarantees(usize capacity,Span<const<AllocationShape>> simultaneous) -> bool` | Whether the complete simultaneous request multiset is within the backed guarantee. |

Geometry queries SHALL use zero allocation and leave FP status unchanged. Boolean queries SHALL return false for invalid/unsupported shapes; Result queries SHALL report InvalidOperation for invalid shape/geometry and ResourceLimit for an unrepresentable charge. The guarantee predicate SHALL be order-independent and account for fragmentation, size classes, alignment, and metadata, with the simultaneous charge sum at most capacity. A successful reservation SHALL back every admitted allocation/release sequence satisfying that predicate.

`SoftQuota(usize limit)` SHALL store an immutable nonreserving limit and expose limit_bytes(). A copied policy SHALL copy that limit. Persistent use SHALL bound each selected BigInt's total retained charge, including replacement preparation; temporary use SHALL bound one TempScope, including its control and live values. Zero SHALL admit total charge zero. Shared aggregate limits SHALL use the selected ResourceRef domain.

`QuotaPolicy` SHALL expose DomainOnly(), Soft(SoftQuota), and Reserved(ReservedQuotaRef). DomainOnly SHALL retain inherited limits. Reserved SHALL share the selected pool and its single occupied-capacity account. Each case SHALL return the stated admission failure through its selected resource contract.

### 3. Plans and their lifetime

`PersistentResources` and `TemporaryResources` SHALL be immutable records constructed from (ResourceRef domain,QuotaPolicy quota), exposing those read-only fields. A Reserved choice SHALL designate a live pool in that exact domain.

`ResourcePlan(PersistentResources persistent,TemporaryResources temporary)` SHALL expose those two read-only fields. Each SHALL retain its distinct accounting role. Explicit references to one reserved pool may share that pool between the roles while preserving its single capacity account.

`default_resource_plan() -> ResourcePlan` SHALL expose the plan bound by the containing definition's resolved numerical contract, including supplying owners and lifetime obligations. Missing required binding SHALL use the central capability diagnostic. Explicit local policies SHALL retain inherited hard limits.

Persistent creation SHALL select its destination plan; assignment SHALL preserve that plan. Copying SHALL use independent destination storage and its selected policy. Ordinary scratch SHALL use the temporary policy and full-expression lifetime unless an explicit scope is supplied. A ResourcePlan SHALL describe those selections; reservation and allocation SHALL occur in their named admission operations.

### 4. ReservedQuota ownership

`QuotaState` SHALL expose Open/Closed. ReservedQuota SHALL own backed capacity and stable charged control state. Default construction SHALL select Closed with an empty record. Move construction SHALL transfer the record, preserve derived-reference identity, and empty the source. Assignment SHALL require Closed destination, retire its old record, and transfer; self-move SHALL preserve state. A failed checked destination precondition SHALL dispatch to ContractTrap before either owner changes.

| Operation | Result and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `try_reserve_quota(ResourceRef domain,usize capacity,GeometryRef geometry)` | NumericResult<ReservedQuota>. |
| `reserve_quota(ResourceRef domain,usize capacity,GeometryRef geometry)` | ReservedQuota or Numeric Trap, with the same admission. |
| `state() -> QuotaState` | Nonallocating observation. |
| `capacity_bytes() -> usize` | Reserved capacity while Open, otherwise zero. |
| `occupied_bytes() -> usize` | Charge currently occupied by allocations within the reservation. |
| `charge_bytes() -> usize` | Actual retained domain charge, including reserved free backing and control storage. |
| `resource() -> Option<ResourceRef>` | Domain while a control record remains, otherwise None. |
| `geometry() -> Option<GeometryRef>` | Geometry while a record remains, otherwise None. |
| `borrow() -> ReservedQuotaRef` | Nonowning pool reference; requires Open. |
| `try_close() -> Result<void,ResourceError>` | Outstanding allocations give Outstanding unchanged; otherwise release backing and become Closed. Already Closed succeeds inertly. |

`ReservedQuotaRef` SHALL be a nonempty copyable borrow exposing state(), capacity_bytes(), occupied_bytes(), resource()->ResourceRef, and geometry()->GeometryRef. It SHALL observe Closed while its record remains live; later use SHALL require that record's valid borrowing interval. Numerical use of Closed SHALL report InvalidOperation before admission.

Reservation admission SHALL establish geometry compatibility, ancestor-budget admission, and actual backing as one transaction under the common model. ResourceLimit and AllocationFailure SHALL retain their distinct identities. An admitted backed shape SHALL receive its advertised allocation guarantee after satisfying independent numerical constraints.

Pool return SHALL lower occupied capacity and retain reserved backing. Close SHALL release backing once; retained control SHALL remain charged through owner retirement. Destruction SHALL require discharged allocations, release remaining backing/control, or dispatch to ContractTrap while unresolved obligations remain.

### 5. Temporary scope and epoch ownership

`TempState` SHALL expose Open/Closed. TempEpoch SHALL identify one scope generation. TempScope(TemporaryResources) SHALL admit its stable epoch/control state and select Open; its value outlet SHALL use NumericTrap on resource failure. TempScope() SHALL select Closed with an empty record. state() SHALL return TempState; epoch() and resources() SHALL return Option<TempEpoch> and Option<TemporaryResources>, selecting None exactly for an empty record. A retained closed record SHALL expose its ended epoch/resources.

A scope SHALL be move-only. Move construction SHALL transfer control, preserve handle epoch identity, and empty the source. Assignment SHALL require Closed destination and retire its old record before transfer; self-move SHALL preserve state. Quiescent close SHALL end the epoch, retire its remaining temporary payloads, and select Closed; repeated close SHALL preserve Closed. Destruction SHALL close and retire the owner's record obligation. Successful transfer SHALL remove the transferred allocation from that cleanup set.

`TempBigInt` SHALL be established by a temporary-result operation as a move-only value/epoch owner. alive() SHALL observe the epoch's open state; epoch() SHALL return its identity. is_zero() SHALL require alive and otherwise dispatch to ContractTrap. A numerical read SHALL validate the selected epoch before accessing its value.

Outstanding handles SHALL retain explicitly charged epoch/control metadata through their final retirement. Scope closure SHALL end values and retire payloads; later handle destruction SHALL retire its metadata obligation. Once the scope owner and all handles have retired those obligations, the metadata SHALL be released. Its resource owner and charge SHALL remain valid through that release.

TempBigInt move SHALL validate source liveness before destination retirement. An expired source SHALL use ContractTrap. Successful movement SHALL transfer the value allocation and leave source zero in its live epoch. Assignment SHALL retire the old destination obligation and adopt the source epoch/value; self-move SHALL preserve state. An expired destination may retire its metadata before assignment. Live-handle destruction SHALL release its remaining allocation and unregister its scope-cleanup obligation. Value duplication SHALL use an explicit persistent Commit or numeric copy operation.

Scope/handle mutation SHALL use declared or external synchronization. Epoch identities SHALL remain distinct while surviving handles can observe their generations. Budget admission SHALL use the common atomic ancestry transaction independently of scope access synchronization.

### 6. Temporary arithmetic catalogue

A and B SHALL independently be BigInt or TempBigInt, borrowed read-only. Fixed/platform operands SHALL first use their explicit family-unification operation.

| Signature family | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `try_temp_add/sub/mul/div/rem<A,B>(TempScope& scope,const<A>& a,const<B>& b)` | NumericResult<TempBigInt>. |
| `temp_add/sub/mul/div/rem<A,B>(TempScope& scope,const<A>& a,const<B>& b)` | TempBigInt or Numeric Trap. |
| The same families without the scope parameter | The same result using the default plan's temporary resources and the enclosing full-expression scope. |

Each slash-separated row SHALL denote the five named declarations. Division/remainder SHALL retain their integer quotient/remainder semantics. After expression evaluation and liveness/policy admission, zero-divisor rejection SHALL precede allocation. Ended scope/operand SHALL report InvalidOperation; exhausted allowance ResourceLimit; failed permitted backing acquisition AllocationFailure.

Success SHALL publish one owning result in the selected epoch. Failure SHALL preserve operands, prior registered temporaries, and committed charges while retiring its uncommitted preparation. The value form SHALL select NumericTrap after the corresponding ordinary Result failure path. Arithmetic status SHALL follow the integer operation; resource administration SHALL contribute an empty FP event set.

The implicit scope SHALL close at the full-expression boundary. A stored handle SHALL then designate its ended epoch, and subsequent Result operations SHALL report expiration. An unintended escape SHALL use the central diagnostic. An explicit scope SHALL keep its epoch open for its own admitted lifetime.

### 7. Commit and exclusive Transfer

| Operation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `try_commit(const<TempBigInt>& temp,ResourcePlan destination)` | NumericResult<BigInt>. |
| `commit(const<TempBigInt>& temp,ResourcePlan destination)` | BigInt or Numeric Trap. |
| `try_transfer(TempBigInt& temp,ResourcePlan destination)` | NumericResult<BigInt>. |
| `transfer(TempBigInt& temp,ResourcePlan destination)` | BigInt or Numeric Trap. |
| Each operation without destination | Same using default_resource_plan(). |

The resulting BigInt SHALL retain the complete destination ResourcePlan. Its persistent field SHALL select result ownership, and its temporary field SHALL select preparation scratch and later temporary computation.

Commit SHALL prepare independent persistent storage and preserve the temporary value, allocation, and epoch. Both live source and prepared result SHALL count during preparation. Zero may use its provider's empty payload representation; a nonzero result SHALL own independent value storage.

Transfer SHALL require exclusive detachable ownership, compatible release/allocator contracts, destination admission, and preserved source reservation backing. It SHALL transfer the existing payload. An allocation-free zero SHALL transfer as zero. Structural incompatibility SHALL report TransferUnavailable; limits ResourceLimit; preparatory backing failure AllocationFailure; expired source InvalidOperation.

Transfer preparation SHALL secure any replacement backing required by source reservations before commitment. Shared ancestors SHALL charge the transferred physical block once; source-only and destination-only accounts SHALL commit their deltas together. Additional prepared backing SHALL contribute its real peak charge. The ownership transaction SHALL retain one current owner and every promised reservation guarantee throughout.

Transfer success SHALL remove the allocation from scope cleanup, establish persistent release obligations, and leave temp zero in its live epoch. Failure SHALL preserve source, destination policy, backing guarantees, and accounting. Commit/Transfer success SHALL report false loss/clamp/wrap/payload-change flags and an empty FP flag set.

Callbacks, failure routing, strong replacement preparation, and profile-specific retirement SHALL use the common library model. This chapter's concrete quota, epoch, and transfer outcomes SHALL be the selected functional state for those operations.
